📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 05:48 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 09:41 EST, 17 November 2026.

Wayne Rooney has revealed how his problems with alcohol left him contemplating suicide during his Manchester United career, as he opened up on the serious impact drinking had on his marriage to wife Coleen.

Rooney, 41, often came across as bullishly confident during his glittering playing career and then in the TV studio as a pundit, but says he is 'lucky' to have survived being thrown into the spotlight as a teenager - when he broke through at Everton at the age of 16.

The scrutiny cast upon him by the watching world led to Rooney hitting 'rock bottom' in his mid-twenties, whereby he recalls locking himself away in his house for two days to 'just drink'.

In a recent development, 'This was at the best part of my career playing wise, I'd go home and sit in my games room and drink for two days,' he said on Life At The Midpoint podcast. 'I'd get up for training, put some eyedrops in and chewing gum, and go to training.

'I couldn't deal with the pressures of everything and I made stupid choices when I was younger, off the pitch, and I really struggled to deal with it all to be honest. It was only when I spoke to Coleen and I spoke to my mum, and I opened up, it was only really when I vocally opened up that I needed help to get through it.

Wayne Rooney has revealed how he contemplated suicide during his 'lowest' moment.

He stated without the support of wife Coleen, he may not have 'survived' as he discussed how his life turned upside down after breaking through as a 16-year-old.

The Man United legend remarked he was binge-drinking for two days at the height of his career.

'When I look back now, you look back with regret because it's time lost. Kai was a baby at the time. I can look back and say I was selfish but I was going through something which I was really struggling to deal with.

According to recent reports, 'I got to a place where I was contemplating suicide. I didn't want to be around anyone, I didn't want to see anybody in the street, in the shops. I was always comfortable on a football pitch, but everything else I struggled with.'.

Rooney added that his drinking problem caused strain on his marriage to childhood sweetheart Coleen, but he couldn't have survived without her help.

'Coleen helped me massively,' Rooney noted. 'I was speaking to a therapist to figure out what was up with me. Looking back, I was at the height of my career, just had a young son, just married, it should have been the happiest moment of my life but it was the lowest, because of the selfish acts I was taking.

Recent findings suggest that 'Coleen was massive. She could have walked away, it was that bad. She stuck by me and helped me get through it and obviously we had more kids.'.

Rooney also spoke candidly about his anxieties over his appearance.

The former Man United and England striker has overhauled his lifestyle, slimmed down, fixed his teeth and undergone a nose job, with fans amazed by his progress.

When asked about how he felt about the prospect of being exposed to a huge audience of viewers in the I'm A Celebrity jungle, Rooney admitted it was something he only now feels comfortable with after his glow-up.

'I wouldn't have been able to do it to be honest with you,' he told Gabby Logan on Life at the Midpoint podcast.

'They asked me last year to go in. I spoke to AngryGinge who I know and Aitch who I know and they were saying, "come in, imagine the three of us in there". It would have been chaos. I didn't think I'd physically be able to do it.

Wayne Rooney, pictured left on I'm a Celebrity and right in 2024, has admitted he used to feel self-conscious about his looks and weight.

Should footballers receive more support for mental health given pressure they face?

'I've always been self-conscious and always been conscious of my weight. I've always thought about how I look.

'Everything has fallen into place now where I know I feel better and know I look better than what I was. I looked at myself about a year ago and thought I did look probably about 50.

Recent findings suggest that 'And I was thinking, "you need to sort yourself out here" and so I was very self-conscious. I have been for my whole career for how I look or my weight, which at times I've struggled with.'.

Rooney had to endure a stomach-churning eating challenge on the launch show on I'm A Celebrity on Monday night, drinking fermented prawns and fish eyes and no doubt there's worse to come.

The slimmed-down Rooney was previously irked that some onlookers thought he had been taking weight loss injections rather than working hard to get in shape.

In a recent development, he previously explained to the Daily Mail: 'Apparently I've seen recently I've been taking this pen thing (weight loss jabs). It's a shame, because I'm working really hard to lose weight. Apparently I've been on the pen.'.

According to recent reports, he added on This Morning: 'I feel great, I haven't drank for a while. I just wanted to feel healthier and be healthier so I've changed my eating habits and training.

'Everyone's saying I'm on this pen thing. but I'm not, I've been working out to try and look better and be healthier.'.

Rooney has been praised for his physical turnaround and is favourite to win the show.

Rooney, pictured two years ago, cut down his drinking and changed his lifestyle.

Recent findings suggest that he also remarked part of the motivation was to feel better for his time with the family. Rooney and his wife, who came second on I'm A Celebrity two years ago, are parents to Kai, 17, Klay, 13, Kit, ten, and Cass, eight.

'I've found more balance, it's helped me get back to a much better place. When I stopped playing, I got in a rut, I was drinking too much and not getting into the routine of training and I just thought, "You know what I want to enjoy the time with the kids whilst they're at this age, and with Coleen as well and I actually have been more present, more there for them,' he added.

At times during his playing days, Rooney was far from the model professional and back in 2012 admitted returning to Man United training seven pounds overweight.

In his book, My Decade in the Premier League, Rooney wrote of the summer of 2009: 'Early July: the first day back at pre-season training. I'm like most blokes, I put on a few pounds after a holiday. Even if I don't train for a week, I put on two or three, but when I get back to Carrington for the first day of work, I'm in for a shock. The scales in the club gym tell me I've put on a few more pounds than expected – seven. Seven!

According to recent reports, 'Then I remember – I drank a few bevvies while I was away. I'm stocky. I'm not like Ryan Giggs, all bone and lean muscle. But I gain weight quite easily. It's not a problem though.

Industry observers note that 'It's not as if the manager is leaning over my shoulder as the numbers come in, tutting and making jokes about me eating too many chip butties. Besides, I know I can shift it in a week or two. All the players are given loose training programmes to stick to while they're away, but they're optional.

'The club like us not to go overboard on the eating and drinking in the close-season break, so if I go abroad I like to get into the hotel gym three times a week to work on the treadmill and do some weight work.

'Coming back for pre-season after a few bevvies and a few weeks away from a ball is physically tough.'.

Despite Rooney's penchant for letting his hair down in the offseason, he was renowned for his work and commitment on the pitch and has recaptured that battling spirit to shed the weight in retirement.

Rooney, pictured during a match against Portugal at the 2006 World Cup in Germany, was not always fully committed to his diet during his glittering playing career.

The England legend has emerged as the betting favourite to be crowned King of the Jungle and is one of the highest-paid contestants in this year's show.

Bosses have reportedly offered Wayne more than his wife, who made a record-breaking £1.5million for her jungle stint.

Last week, Rooney mentioned: 'This is probably the biggest exposure I've ever had, being on TV every night for three weeks.

'I hope people see I am a genuine person,' adding that he is a 'fun guy' who enjoys 'pranks'.

No doubt his dieting will be beneficial in having to deal with rations of long grain rice and beans in Australia for the duration of the show.

The AC Milan squad returned to training at Milanello on Monday, at least those who are not with their national team.

This morning’s edition of La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) has provided an update on the various injuries that have massively depleted the depth available to head coach Ruben Amorim in the past few weeks.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Starting with Mike Maignan, both he and the French medical staff have reassured Milan regarding the physical problem that forced the goalkeeper to be substituted at half-time during Sunday’s match between Les Bleus and Turkey.

According to recent reports, the Rossoneri captain took a knock to the hip area and felt some discomfort in his right adductor. No medical examinations were conducted while he was away, but they have been scheduled for early this afternoon.

Maignan has put the club at ease, stating that he is not in any pain. Yesterday evening, he posted a photo of himself preparing to make a save, perhaps a way of saying he is ready. However, Lorenzo Torriani is on stand-by if needed.

Meanwhile, yesterday afternoon, Fikayo Tomori and Ruben Loftus-Cheek underwent examinations to assess their recovery from their respective muscle injuries. The tests took place in London, where both players spent the week off granted by the coaching staff.

The news is encouraging, and the recovery process is progressing well: the injury to the defender’s medial flexor in his right thigh is healing, and he will begin gradual work on the pitch over the coming days.

Sources indicate that whether he will be available against Frosinone or for the Europa League match against Olympiakos remains to be seen. The injury sustained against Bologna in late October is nearly behind him, but no unnecessary risks will be taken.

Industry News: £1.2m Blackburn Rovers man has a chance to lock down a starting spot, beginning with crucial Burnley tie: Opinion

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (627 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, blackburn Rovers face Burnley in a Lancashire derby on Sunday.
  • Industry observers note that damien Johnson and Mike Dodds will lead the side on an interim basis, but the temporary bosses will not be able to call upon star right-back Ryan Alebiosu.
  • It has been revealed that summer signing Gady Beyuku replaced Alebiosu when he hobbled off against Stoke City.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, blackburn Rovers face Burnley in a Lancashire derby on Sunday. It’s a substantial occasion at Ewood Park, not only because of the rivalry, but because it marks Rovers’ first game since Tony Mowbray stepped back as head coach due to health issues earlier this week.

Industry observers note that damien Johnson and Mike Dodds will lead the side on an interim basis, but the temporary bosses will not be able to call upon star right-back Ryan Alebiosu. The Nigerian international has undergone surgery on his knee and is set to be sidelined until the Newly introduced Year.

It has been revealed that summer signing Gady Beyuku replaced Alebiosu when he hobbled off against Stoke City. And, he played the full 90 minutes against West Ham while the medical staff waited for a verdict on Alebiosu’s blow.

Now that we know how long Blackburn Rovers’ go-to right-back will be out for, Beyuku has a real chance to make the starting role his own.

Industry observers note that most clubs have at least two players to cover in every position, and that is the case at Blackburn Rovers. With Alebiosu out, Beyuku is the only natural senior right-back available for selection, paving the way for him to come into the side.

It has been revealed that A reported fee of around £1.2m was paid to sign the 20-year-old from Modena in the summer, so there is clear belief in his potential. It was widely expected that Beyuku would be cover and competition for Alebiosu, but the injury thrusts him into the limelight.

Industry observers note that he’s shown signs of growing into Championship football early on as well. His second-half against West Ham was the best we’ve seen from Beyuku to date, offering a lively presence up and down the right-hand side.

According to recent reports, the Frenchman saw to his duties at the back with 10 defensive contributions, but he was forward-thinking and frequently involved in possession like Alebiosu as well. Beyuku completed 26 of his 29 passes, nine of which were line-breaking.

He was dispossessed twice, but this does come with the territory of being a progressive right-back who is still developing and settling into a latest league (all stats via FotMob).

Alebiosu’s shoes are substantial ones to fill. It might not have been planned that Beyuku would assume a starting role this early into his Blackburn Rovers, given his age and need to grow into Championship football.

It means that, despite the fact he needs to deliver, there should be an element of patience.

Sources indicate that if Johnson and Dodds feel Beyuku needs to be taken out of the side, there are options to consider. Kristi Montgomery has a key role in midfield alongside Sam Morsy but he has covered at right-back before. Matty Litherland is working his way back from injury too, while Lewis Miller is a longer-term absentee.

Beyuku will have the firm backing of the Rovers faithful. A strong display against arch-rivals Burnley this Sunday would be a sure-fire way for the youngster to endear himself to the fans and announce himself in Championship football.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After failing to complete their defence in the final days of the summer transfer window, AC Milan will try again in January.

The defensive depth is rather limited amid Matteo Gabbia’s lengthy injury absence, while Fikayo Tomori also sustained an problem, meaning a reinforcement in that area of ​​the pitch will be needed in January. Ruben Amorim’s number one target has not changed from the summer.

Recent findings suggest that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

This morning’s edition of Corriere dello Sport (via MilanNews) confirms the No.1 centre-back target: Goncalo Inacio. Milan tried to snatch him from Sporting CP in August, but the Portuguese club repeatedly turned them down, having already sold Ousmane Diomande to Nottingham Forest.

Sources indicate that the Rossoneri haven’t abandoned the idea of ​​reuniting him with Amorim, and so in January they will make another attempt for the 25-year-old, who is eager to join a top club. However, a significant offer of at least €40m will be needed to convince Sporting.

According to recent reports, the management believe that another central defender is needed too, so they’re starting to monitor some prospects for next summer. Among the players being closely monitored is Gabriele Calvani, who is on loan at Frosinone from Genoa.

In a recent development, he has impressed so far and has a current valuation of €10m that could rise. For now, signing a young prospect isn’t a priority for the Rossoneri, as they are primarily looking for someone who can slot immediately into the starting XI.

Chelsea's Malo Gusto named 'biggest disappointment of the Zidane era'... and Liverpool's £123m man Bradley Barcola 'lacked accuracy and composure' in damning verdict on France's Premier League stars

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (548 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 06:01 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 11:31 EST, 17 November 2026.
  • The French media have come down hard on a number of Premier League players in the national team after less than impressive displays under upcoming coach Zinedine Zidane.
  • Over the break France scraped a 2-1 win against Turkey in the Nations League but only after an unexpected 3-1 loss to Italy at the San Siro.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 06:01 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 11:31 EST, 17 November 2026.

The French media have come down hard on a number of Premier League players in the national team after less than impressive displays under upcoming coach Zinedine Zidane.

Over the break France scraped a 2-1 win against Turkey in the Nations League but only after an unexpected 3-1 loss to Italy at the San Siro.

And among the team's most glaring underperformers – according to some observers in France – were Chelsea's Malo Gusto, Bournemouth's Adrien Truffert and Liverpool's £123million summer signing Bradley Barcola.

French outlet RMC Sport was particularly critical of the pair, with journalist Alexandre Jaquin describing Gusto as 'probably the one who disappointed the most during this second international window of the Zidane era'.

Jaquin added: 'Fielded in Italy despite little playing time with Chelsea, the right-back completely fell into the San Siro furnace.

Malo Gusto struggled has been under fire from the French media after a string of poor performances under Zinedine Zidane.

The honeymoon period is over for Zidane, according to French media.

Recent findings suggest that 'Overwhelmed by his opponents' energy and little helped by Michael Olise's lack of defensive defense, the former Lyon player lived a nightmare in Lombardy, notably conceding a penalty. A match rapidly erased from his memory.'.

RMC was not much kinder to Barcola as well, concluding: 'The Liverpool winger was one of the few to start both matches in November. But in the end, it didn't really take off, neither in Italy nor against Turkey.

'Sometimes on his left flank, sometimes in a false nine, the former PSG supersub was often imprecise in his final moves. Like his failed one-on-one against the Turks, the Lyon native lacked accuracy and composure to make the opposing goal tremble.'.

Industry observers note that even newcomer Adrien Truffert was not afforded some sympathy as Jaquin said: 'After a rather satisfying debut in October, the Bournemouth left-back benefited from the trust of Zinedine Zidane, who played him in Italy. But despite his efforts, the Cherries player delivered a very mixed performance.'.

This recent criticism adds to growing dissatisfaction in France with the overall state of the national team under Zidane.

Liverpool's £123million man is yet to make a major impact for club or country so far this season.

Calafiori has a shot from 18 yards blocked after a typical run infield from left-back.

It has been revealed that arsenal have started well and are dominating possession. So far it’s all been in front of the Sunderland defence, but you’d expect that to change if they continue to have this much of the ball.

The champions kick off from left to right as we watch.

There’s a pulsating atmosphere at the Stadium of Light - you’d expect nothing less - and the action is about to begin.

Myles Lewis Skelly is the first England teenager to start the first four league games of a season for Arsenal since Tony Adams and David Rocastle in the 1986/87 campaign.

According to recent reports, we’re in a congested period right now. We’re playing midweek games as well. We made four changes against Napoli, we make another four for today and we try to keep all the players connected with a high level of confidence, and with the right chemistry in and around the team.

Sources indicate that we know how tough Sunderland made it for every opponent here [last season] and we know the beautiful atmosphere that they create, the organisation that they have and the individuals that they have. We’ll try to impose ourselves like we always do and come here and be as dominant as we’ve been and then be ready to win the game.

Recent findings suggest that arsenal’s biggest rivals are still waiting for their first win - and their first goal - of the Premier League season. Alex Connor has reaction to their 0-0 draw at home to Everton.

"For sure we can improve, and we will" 😅Mikel Arteta on Arsenal's strong start to the season 🗣️📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nDpwooZq4Y.

Arsenal keeper David Raya has conceded only one goal in five matches this season, but he was beaten twice on this ground last season during a thrilling 2-2 draw.

Recent findings suggest that when will Martin Zubimendi start again for Arsenal? Mikel Arteta wants to avoid a repeat of last season, when Zubimendi played more games than anyone in Europe, but it is curious that the Spaniard has not yet started a single match of this campaign. It is one thing to reduce his minutes, and another to turn him into a permanent substitute.

Sources indicate that zubimendi has looked quite good off the bench in recent games but has been behind Myles Lewis-Skelly and Mikel Merino in the battle to partner Declan Rice from the start. And that’s before Bruno Guimaraes, the new £75m signing, reaches full fitness.

In the thick Naples air in midweek, Declan Rice did what he always does: he kept running. Another start for the Arsenal midfielder, another 90 minutes completed and another performance of constructive passing and destructive defending. For anyone who was worried about Rice’s physical condition, it was an emphatic response.

It has been revealed that after that Champions League victory over Napoli, Rice insisted he was ready for another marathon campaign. He made 69 appearances for club and country last season, up from 60 the previous term, and believes that is a sustainable number of games, even for an all-action midfielder such as himself. “I have shown I can do it,” he remarked.

It has been revealed that the key question, though, is not whether Rice can do it, but whether he should do it. There is no doubt that his body eventually began to pay the price for his exertions last year, especially during the World Cup, and it would be reasonable for his managers to worry that his extraordinary workload might one day take a serious toll. This, after all, is a footballer who managed nerve pain in his hamstring throughout the second half of last season.

Regis Le Bris, who made 11 changes for the League Cup win over Hull in midweek, reverts to the starting XI that drew at Brentford seven days ago.

RLB's XI to take on Arsenal! ❤️👊#SUNARS pic.twitter.com/F1nXWky4Fp.

Industry observers note that mikel Arteta has made four changes to the Arsenal team that won in Napoli during the week. Kai Havertz’s return is the headline news in Arteta’s selection, with in-form left-back Riccardo Calafiori also returning. Myles Lewis-Skelly returns to the midfield and Christos Tzolis starts.

Hello and welcome to live, minute-by-minute coverage of Sunderland v Arsenal at the Stadium of Light. Sunderland are the latest team tasked with stopping Arsenal, who have begun their title defence in formidable style: they’ve won out of three, including a dominant comeback victory against Chelsea last weekend, and look well equipped to become the first Arsenal team to retain the title since the mid-1930s.

Recent findings suggest that there’s a long way to go, and Arsenal fans will remember how blisteringly they started their last two title defences in 2002-03 and 2004-05, only to ultimately fall short. But right now, they could barely be in better shape. Their fine start to the season came with a Champions League win in Naples, achieved despite a delay to their flight from London.

In a recent development, “I love those challenges,” noted Mikel Arteta. “I try to create them in pre-seasons so when they happen, we already experience them and we already know. So get to the stadium very late, change the routine and suddenly the players have to do something else.

Recent findings suggest that “Because when it happens, and it can happen, you can miss the flight, the train can be delayed, there’s so much traffic and I don’t want the players, but not only the players, the staff as well, panicking. So when that happens, adapt to it.”.

According to recent reports, arteta has tested his squad in a variety of ways. “[We have] delayed the meals, delayed the transport, taken a different route. We’ve done many things – made the dressing room hotter, more difficult, more challenging, less beds... because we’re going to have to adapt to different contexts.”.

So far, they’re adapting very well to the context of being the reigning champions.

Declan Rice has agreed a new five-year deal at Arsenal that will run until the summer of 2031 - with goalkeeper David Raya set to join him in committing his future to the club.

Sources indicate that the England midfielder is expected to sign the new contract soon, which is set to put him alongside Bukayo Saka as Arsenal's top earner. Saka is on a deal worth over £350,000 a week.

Recent findings suggest that and Raya, 31, is understood to have agreed a deal in principle to extend his terms. Both players' existing deals expire in 2028.

Rice joined Arsenal in 2023 for £105million from West Ham and has established himself as the fulcrum of their midfield, helping steer them to the Premier League title last season.

The 27-year-old played 55 games in all competitions last season as the Gunners reached their first Champions League final since 2006, but lost out to Paris Saint-Germain.

His contract talks have been ongoing from at least March and are now finalised.

Raya joined Arsenal from Brentford on loan in the same summer, and signed a permanent deal a year later.

Declan Rice has agreed a latest-five year deal at Arsenal that will run until the summer of 2031.

David Raya has agreed a deal in principle to stay on, with his current deal expiring in 2028.

Rice had confirmed a upcoming deal was close over the weekend when speaking on international duty with England.

'I've been extremely lucky that I've managed to play at such a consistent level throughout my career.

'I've always been stable in the clubs I've been at.

'A new contract is hopefully on the horizon soon.

'I'm extremely lucky that I'm at a club like Arsenal, where my manager [Mikel Arteta] and my team-mates put so much energy in me.

'I'm extremely lucky I don't have to think about that stuff.'.

Derby County & West Ham must provide Southampton escape route for Man City star

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Southampton have fought their way back up the Championship table and into play-off contention despite a four-point deduction at the start of the season, as head coach Tonda Eckert may already have one eye on the upcoming January transfer window.

In what is now old news, Southampton were deducted four points at the start of the Championship campaign after being found guilty of spying on opponents last season, and were also thrown out of the play-offs as a result.

This time around, the Saints are looking to claw their way into the top eight legitimately with Eckert still at the helm, and following eight wins, four draws, and three defeats after 15 league games, they are well within play-off contention.

The German boss has stamped his authority at St Mary's following the summer transfer window, though not every addition has necessarily worked out the way he would've hoped.

Southampton saw the likes of Shea Charles, Taylor Harwood-Bellis, Cameron Archer, and Ben Brereton Diaz head out of the St Mary's exit door over the summer, as the likes of Lewis Dobbin, James Ward-Prowse, Keven Schlotterbeck, and Divin Mubama joined in the opposite direction.

Mubama, 21, joined on loan from Manchester City after spending the previous campaign on loan with Stoke City in the Championship, with the England youth international expecting to push Canadian striker Cyle Larin hard for a place in the starting XI.

Divin Mubama Stoke City Championship statistics 2025/26 (Data as per FotMob).

However, despite his 13 league appearances thus far, only one of those has come as a start, with Mubama being limited to just over 200 minutes of league football so far this campaign, struggling to make an impact in those limited minutes.

Naturally, his parent club, Man City, won't be pleased by his lack of game time and subsequent development, as Football League World has taken a look at two Championship clubs that should consider rescuing the 21-year-old this winter.

Derby County find themselves in the midst of a scrap towards the foot of the Championship table as things stand, with two wins, four draws, and nine defeats in their opening 15 league games piling pressure on head coach John Eustace.

A 3-1 home victory over Bolton Wanderers just before the international break has seemingly given Eustace a lifeline at Pride Park, and if his side can start to pick up some form, he may well start turning his attention to the January transfer window sooner rather than later.

Up top, Derby can boast the likes of Carlton Morris, Henrik Meister, and Lars-Jorgen Salvesen, whilst both Patrick Agyemang, Mohammed Fuseini, and Rhian Brewster can also operate in that position; on the face of it, a new centre-forward option is not needed.

However, those six options have just five goals between them at this stage in the season, and whilst numerous factors can be attributed to this, Derby simply cannot afford to settle with what they have got.

The Rams, according to Pete O'Rourke via X, were closing in on a move for Mubama earlier on in the summer window, but for one reason or another, the deal never went through, and the England youth international headed to Southampton instead.

The sort of centre-forward that Eustace loves: quick, strong, capable of holding up the ball and interlinking play as well as getting in behind, and with smart movement, Mubama would be an excellent addition for Derby, and if he can be provided with chances regularly, he will help the Rams look towards the play-offs instead of the relegation zone.

Recent findings suggest that would you like to see Divin Mubama at your club? Do you agree with our picks? Where do you think he should go? Share your thoughts below!

Mubama spent the bulk of his youth playing days in the West Ham United academy, going on to make 18 first-team appearances for the Hammers and scoring once before heading to Man City in the summer of 2024 for just £1.2 million compensation.

West Ham have endured a tricky start to life back in the Championship, with Nuno Espírito Santo being handed his marching orders after 13 games and being replaced by former Fulham, Bournemouth, and Burnley boss Scott Parker.

Parker made over a century of appearances for the East London outfit during his playing days, and it is hoped that he can steer the club in the right direction following his appointment.

The former England midfielder may well already have one eye on the January transfer window, with Alan Nixon having recently reported via Patreon that West Ham are targeting a fresh striker and left-back this winter.

Taty Castellanos and Pablo Felipe have not handled the drop into the second tier especially well, as Joel Piroe has emerged as the preferred option up front as things stand, though the Dutchman could do with some competition.

As a cheap loan, and a player who understands exactly what the West Ham DNA is, Mubama would be a solid fit for the Hammers and would offer a completely different profile to Piroe.

If Castellanos and Pablo leave, a newly introduced striker will be needed regardless, and following his lack of minutes with Southampton, Parker has the opportunity to show the Saints exactly what they've been missing out on with a January swoop.

Roberto Di Matteo lifts lid on West Brom decision that shocked him

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (582 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Roberto Di Matteo has admitted that he was ‘shocked’ West Brom sacked him back in 2011 as they battled to stay in the Premier League.
  • The Italian had a successful playing career, and he turned to management after retiring, initially starting out with MK Dons.
  • A move to Albion would follow, and Di Matteo would also work for Chelsea, Schalke and Aston Villa, with the high point undoubtedly coming with the Blues, who he won the Champions League and FA Cup with as interim boss.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Roberto Di Matteo has admitted that he was ‘shocked’ West Brom sacked him back in 2011 as they battled to stay in the Premier League.

The Italian had a successful playing career, and he turned to management after retiring, initially starting out with MK Dons.

A move to Albion would follow, and Di Matteo would also work for Chelsea, Schalke and Aston Villa, with the high point undoubtedly coming with the Blues, who he won the Champions League and FA Cup with as interim boss.

Whilst nothing will surpass winning those trophies with Chelsea, Di Matteo really made his name as a manager during his time at The Hawthorns with West Brom.

After making the step up from League One outfit MK Dons, Di Matteo built an Albion side that won promotion to the Premier League in his first season at the club.

They did so by playing a brand of football that the fans really enjoyed, and they carried that into the top flight. Whilst an opening day 6-0 defeat at Chelsea was concerning, the players quickly adapted to the Premier League.

The Baggies had picked up 15 points from their first nine games, which included a memorable 3-2 win at Arsenal, a 2-2 draw at Old Trafford, and they also picked up a point from Tottenham.

So, Albion were performing very well, and they continued the entertaining style of play that had made them such a good watch the season before.

However, that form didn’t continue, and Di Matteo was ultimately dismissed in February, after a miserable period of seven defeats in nine.

And, speaking to Mick McCarthy and Tony Pulis on The Managers podcast, Di Matteo couldn’t hide how disappointed he was at the decision, with Albion outside the relegation zone at the time.

“I was a bit surprised and shocked. We’ve all worked in smaller clubs, so when you have injuries to one or two key players, it’s difficult. Up until the Christmas period we were looking really good, but Jonas Olsson, the centre-back, got injured for a while, and one or two others were not available.

Recent findings suggest that “In the Christmas period, you play every two or three days and you don’t have a deep squad, so you struggle a bit. But, again, we were coming out of it, and I was really shocked.”.

You can understand why Di Matteo was surprised at the decision, as he will have been tasked with keeping the team in the league, and he will argue he was on track to do that.

Plus, this was the first tough spell he had in charge of Albion, so he would’ve hoped that he had enough credit in the bank to be given an opportunity to turn things around.

Yet, football is a ruthless business, and the Albion board needed to make what they felt was the best decision for the club, and the reality is that, in hindsight, it was a call that paid off.

They had been on a terrible run over a period of a few months, and they would say the trend was pointing towards relegation.

West Brom fans, how do you reflect on Roberto Di Matteo's time in charge? Let us know in the comments below.

As it turns out, West Brom appointed Roy Hodgson, in what was a masterstroke. He kept the team up with ease, and they had another seven consecutive years as a Premier League before relegation in 2018.

Gary Neville debuts surprise defence of Diogo Dalot and names the THREE defenders Mauricio Pochettino should sell before Man United boo boy

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1211 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 10:42 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 12:38 EST, 17 November 2026.
  • Gary Neville has stood up for under-fire Manchester United man Diogo Dalot – and named three of his defensive team-mates he would rather see leave the club before him.
  • The Portugal international's limp performances have come under heavy scrutiny this season with the decline of Michael Carrick's side as autumn has worn on.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 10:42 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 12:38 EST, 17 November 2026.

Gary Neville has stood up for under-fire Manchester United man Diogo Dalot – and named three of his defensive team-mates he would rather see leave the club before him.

The Portugal international's limp performances have come under heavy scrutiny this season with the decline of Michael Carrick's side as autumn has worn on.

But as Mauricio Pochettino prepares to take over at Old Trafford, Neville urged the new manager not to immediately expel the defender, despite his drop-off in form.

'I think if he was in a decent back four he'd be alright,' Neville told Stick to United co-host Mark Goldbridge on Tuesday. 'But he's got a shocking back four alongside him.

'Positionally he's not great. He could be better on the ball. He could be better at everything he does. Of course he could. I just think he's such an easy target, Dalot. I honestly do.'.

Neville admitted that sometimes he listens to his fellow Man United-supporting friends deriding Dalot and wonders 'are they watching something that I don't see?'.

Gary Neville has defended Man United star Diogo Dalot - arguing that he has team-mates who are far weaker.

The Portugal international has come in for heavy criticism from supporters this season.

But in his opinion, there are three defenders that he would let go in the 'first wave' of changes in Manchester.

'I'd be getting (Noussair) Mazraoui well gone before him,' he continued. 'I'd be getting (Lisandro) Martinez gone well before him. I'll be getting (Matthijs) De Ligt gone well before him.

Sources indicate that '(De Ligt has) got one significant problem. He doesn’t play football. If a player is injury prone and doesn't play football, just because he hasn't played doesn't mean to say that he should go above a player who's played every single week and he's throwing his hand up. You want someone who's actually reliable and play. De Ligt has to go. De Ligt, Martinez, Mazraoui.'.

Another stalwart in the team that Neville was keen to have a second chance under Pochettino was Luke Shaw.

'He will keep Shaw because he knows him and he'll probably get the best out of him. The problem with Luke is injuries,' he added. 'So he'll have to manage him. So he'll have to bring a left back in. But let's just say who he'll keep.

'He'll keep Shaw. He'll keep (Harry) Maguire because he'll trust him and he'll think that he's basically a soldier and someone who can do a job for him.

Industry observers note that 'He'll keep (Leny) Yoro because I think he'll think "I've got something there that I can work with". (But) I think he's a little bit gangly, all over the place right now. And he looks like he's going to slip every time. He's got that sort of Bambi-on-ice (look).

According to recent reports, 'Physically what will happen is with Yoro, he'll go one way or the other. I like the fact he's been brought into the French team. It tells me sometimes you just have got to connect the dots and think, "okay, well, if they think he's good, then we must be missing something here because we're not seeing it yet, are we?".'.

Neville went on to suggest that Yoro was lacking the connection within his body that Premier League rivals such as Jeremy Jacquet are already able to harness – something Sir Alex Ferguson had identified in Rio Ferdinand when he was at West Ham.

Like Ferdinand, Neville backed Yoro to flourish as he taps into that connection and improves his strength and stability.

In a recent development, 'So Yoro he will keep: Yoro, Maguire and Shaw I think he'll keep and I think he'll keep Dalot. To start with,' Neville said. 'He'll have to bring in three defenders to go above them. Let's be clear. He'll have to bring in three defenders.

Sources indicate that 'Mazraoui I would lose, De Ligt I would lose because he's injury prone. Martinez 100 per cent. 100 per cent. 100 per cent.'.

As well as struggling for form this season, Martinez has been a challenging presence in the Man United squad this term, boldly calling out the Man United hierarchy during a firebrand interview last month.

Neville was more interested in fresh head coach Mauricio Pochettino despatching Noussair Mazraoui and Matthijs de Ligt.

Lisandro Martinez has been an unsettled presence in the side this season and hit out at the club's recruiting last month.

The Argentina star implied that he was disappointed with the club's recruitment strategy over the summer, and was forced to hold clear-the-air talks to smooth his return to the side.

Neville added that he would send Ayden Heaven on loan to get experience in the lower divisions to 'build' his ability up, as it was borderline 'unfair' to be 'putting him in' the side at present.

But not all of the changes can come rapidly for Pochettino, who has little time before taking charge of Man United against Liverpool at Anfield this weekend.

According to recent reports, 'First wave, end of the season,' Neville clarified of what he believes Pochettino's strategy for change will be. 'No, he can't get rid of (them all) in January.

'He has to bring one or two defenders in January if he can. But he can't get rid of all those in his first wave. He's only got one month till January.'.

The drawn-out process of sacking Carrick began last week when Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada flew to Monaco for talks with co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer ownership group.

While his future was on the chopping block, Carrick held training sessions at Carrington before the axe finally swung last Thursday.

Pochettino was appointed days later and gave a tearful farewell press conference ahead of his penultimate game with the United States national team on Saturday.

‘I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,’ he told the press. ‘It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

‘When these moments arrive, it is always tough. Normally it is the opposite – you have been sacked! You cry because you want to stay. I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

Recent findings suggest that ‘Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

It has been revealed that ‘In some part it’s a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'.

Birmingham City's latest £1.2bn stadium has a 135-year-old secret

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Birmingham City's 2026/27 season has got off to a remarkable start on the pitch, with supporters starting to dream about what might be possible under Chris Davies.
  • The 41-year-old previously split opinion amongst Blues fans, especially after the way in which the 2025/26 Championship season panned out following continued investment from Knighthead Capital Management.
  • The club's American investors have vowed to change plenty in such a short space of time, and that doesn't just concern the outlook of Davies' squad in the near future as they chase a Premier League return, but the city of Birmingham as a whole.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Birmingham City's 2026/27 season has got off to a remarkable start on the pitch, with supporters starting to dream about what might be possible under Chris Davies.

The 41-year-old previously split opinion amongst Blues fans, especially after the way in which the 2025/26 Championship season panned out following continued investment from Knighthead Capital Management.

The club's American investors have vowed to change plenty in such a short space of time, and that doesn't just concern the outlook of Davies' squad in the near future as they chase a Premier League return, but the city of Birmingham as a whole.

Tom Wagner has been heralded for the work he has already put in and what he is planning towards as Blues look to finally realise their potential.

The idea of looking at the past to move forward can often be frowned upon, but for Wagner and Co. doing exactly that means that Birmingham fans are never likely to lose sight of their identity as the club embarks on a new era.

Last season may have been one of mixed fortunes for Birmingham and their supporters on the pitch, but that didn't mean it wasn't historic in other ways.

Indeed, just days before Blues celebrated their 150th anniversary game with a 4-1 rout over Norwich City, the club unveiled the design and name of its upcoming 62,500-seater stadium, which will stand tall less than a mile away from St. Andrew's @ Knighthead Park.

The Powerhouse will pay tribute to the Second City's rich industrial heritage, embodied by its name and design, and that comes across in more ways than one.

The Powerhouse will be the centrepiece of a multi-billion Sports Quarter project that will transform the Bordesley Green area with multiple commercial and retail hubs adjacent to the stadium.

Whilst the chimney-themed design has received major criticism from rival fanbases and beyond, those associated with the club will love how it will repurpose some of Birmingham's rich history.

Over 1,000 bricks which helped structure the City Hospital in Winson Green - built in 1912 as Birmingham Workhouse Infirmary - are being repurposed for the Powerhouse to stand tall on the former site of the Adderley Park Brickworks.

In a recent development, blues fans, how excited are you to move into the Powerhouse? Comment below!

City Hospital has been closed since 2024, with the former site making way for a 750-home development adjacent to the Birmingham and Wolverhampton Main Line Canal, approximately 4.1 miles away from St. Andrew's.

"Lovingly salvaged, cleaned, sorted and restored by local experts, the original bricks from Adderley Park Brickworks will be incorporated into the Powerhouse – Birmingham City's future home and a defining part of the city’s Sports Quarter," a section of a statement on Blues' website confirming the purchase of remarked bricks read.

In recent months, more work has gone into how the overall Sports Quarter and the Powerhouse stadium will look ahead of a planned opening in the summer of 2031.

Many Blues fans are excited by what is to come, as emotional as it will be when the club have to leave St. Andrew's, having called their current stadium home since the year 1906.

In May, mutiple 'CGI' images were generated and shared by Birmingham's official social media accounts, including how various hospitality packages will be incorporated into the chimney designs.

This includes a high-level view of the pitch which will be named the 'Chimney Seats', as well as 'Restaurant with a View', which will allow guests a view of the city's main skyline, which stands approximately two miles away.

As previously mentioned, Knighthead have certainly done their utmost to embrace themselves in various cultural aspects associated with the West Midlands.

The Sports Quarter will provide thousands of jobs for locals, whilst also increasing the economy. In the meantime, the investment firm has also acquired stakes in Birmingham Phoenix alongside former Blues academy graduate and Real Madrid star, Jude Bellingham.

It has been revealed that the effort which has gone into such a transformative project has not been underestimated by Blues fans, and it has been particularly evident how they feel about Wagner in his recent returns to St. Andrew's after unfortunately suffering a stroke in January.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Charlie Austin believes Blackburn Rovers will be determined to beat Burnley for Tony Mowbray when the two rivals meet on Sunday.

It has been a tough few days for Rovers, as the club unveiled that Mowbray had stepped back from his role as head coach due to health issues.

Many had tipped Blackburn for relegation before a ball was kicked this season, but they have enjoyed a very positive campaign so far under Mowbray, with the team going into the weekend fixtures just three points outside the play-off places.

Therefore, news of Mowbray’s health complications is a real setback for the club, although it obviously puts football into perspective, with the football world coming together to wish the ex-Middlesbrough chief well.

And, speaking on his Chaz Kicks Off podcast, former Burnley striker Austin echoed those thoughts, and he also explained why the news will unite the Rovers group going into the game.

“When anybody gets ill, or has issues in their personal life, you wish them all the best. But you see from all the players and people that know him, that have made comments, it reveals what kind of bloke he is.

Recent findings suggest that “Blackburn’s teamtalk is done. It’s an easy one to say, let’s win this for the manager, let’s win it for Mowbray. He’s got more key things going on in his life, which puts football second, but let's go and give everything. Not 110%, but as a collective, let's give 150% and go and run over our neighbours Burnley and make a big statement.

“That’s how I’d see it if I was in the Blackburn dressing room, and it’d be the same if I was a coach or a fan - go and put on a performance for Mowbray.”.

This news came as a shock to the Rovers supporters, so it presumably was the same for the players, and, as Austin states, the initial reaction is to send your thoughts to Mowbray.

But, football will go on, and it’s inevitable that the Blackburn group will want to get results for the manager, as he was a hugely respected figure at the club, and he has personally helped so many of the current squad.

It’s not like they need extra motivation to beat Burnley when you consider the hatred that comes with the East Lancashire derby anyway, but, if they did, then this will provide it, and you can be sure that Mowbray’s name will be spoken about before the players go out on Sunday.

Of course, the coaching staff won’t want to add too much emotional pressure to the players, so they must channel it properly, but the Blackburn squad will head to Turf Moor with full belief that they can pick up three points.

This is a fixture that the Clarets have dominated recently, with Burnley having not lost to their rivals in the last 11 attempts, which is a run that stretches back to 2010.

What are your predictions for Burnley vs Blackburn? Let us know in the comments below.

But, with Burnley’s terrible season so far, and the fact they’ve not won at home in over a year, this is a fantastic chance for Blackburn, and they will hope to make it a special day for the club by winning on Sunday.

Latest Update: Woeful Man Utd have no excuses, Carrick is under massive pressure

💡 Key Takeaways
  • This was a kick in the midriff for Manchester United.
  • They profited from the first one with Phil Foden sent off after hitting out at Bruno Fernandes – in retaliation – after he was booted in the backside by the United captain who somehow went unpunished.
  • In a recent development, but then City played three quarters of this 199th Manchester derby with just 10 men and came out on top with the inevitable and outstanding Erling Haaland scoring his ninth goal against United to become the top scorer in Premier League meetings between these rivals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This was a kick in the midriff for Manchester United. Not once. But twice. And, then, most painfully, a third time with a dismal, dispiriting defeat.

They profited from the first one with Phil Foden sent off after hitting out at Bruno Fernandes – in retaliation – after he was booted in the backside by the United captain who somehow went unpunished.

In a recent development, but then City played three quarters of this 199th Manchester derby with just 10 men and came out on top with the inevitable and outstanding Erling Haaland scoring his ninth goal against United to become the top scorer in Premier League meetings between these rivals. And that was a far more painful and damaging blow.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy.

On a day in which thousands of fans protested, accusing co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers – with Avram Glazer joining Ratcliffe in attendance – of treating them like “s---”, United unfortunately left a nasty whiff of being just that out on the pitch.

United were frankly, woeful. They lacked belief and imagination and attacking instinct and too many of their players – their apparent massive players – went missing when they needed to stand up and take the game by the scruff of the neck. They could not break down City’s defence and failed to be a front-foot team who can dominate the ball. Which is surely what they aspire to be?

Industry observers note that they hit the post twice – through Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo – with efforts from 25 yards. And those two local lads were by far their best players. Without them, United carried so little threat, were so blunt, that it was shocking.

Industry observers note that the question for Michael Carrick, the Manchester United head coach, is simple: what is he trying to do with this team? Can they only ever depend on counter-attacks?

Afterwards Haaland talked about City’s “personality, character” and that was exactly what United lacked. They did not adapt a tactical proposal to combat 10-man City’s desire to keep their wingers high and wide, and break with intent and still try and attack.

Sources indicate that it was telling that so little did City’s new head coach Enzo Maresca worry about United that he did not add a defensive player, and when he took off Rayan Cherki at half-time, he replaced him with the equally creative Iliman Ndiaye who impressed. Maresca knew United needed space to run in behind and denied them that. It was that simple.

City also struck the post with United goalkeeper Senne Lammens tipping an Enzo Fernández shot against the frame of the goal, and the visitors were worthy winners as they preserved their perfect start to the season to draw level on points with leaders, Arsenal.

City handled the occasion and the – admittedly toothless – opposition superbly under their new head coach and will clearly be Arsenal’s closest challengers this season.

Maresca delivered a masterclass. For Carrick? This was a disasterclass. An object lesson in how not to use a man-advantage. And now United will have to endure even more City songs after being outplayed at home like this.

Was it complacency? Was it inability? Was it a damning lack of courage, confidence, belief even? On the pitch and in the dugout United were far too passive. This was not how a significant team plays and Carrick needs to wake up.

The former midfielder did so well last season to guide United into Champions League qualification but so far this campaign he has given the impression that his job is done. Rather than that the real work starts now.

According to recent reports, there was controversy around the red card and the goal. There is no doubt Foden had to go. But what about Fernandes? He clearly kicked Foden as he was on the ground with the midfielder reacting instinctively, two-footing him in the gut.

It meant he became the first City player to be dismissed in a Manchester derby in the league since Bernardo Corradi in December 2006 and will be punished with a three-match ban for violent conduct.

To make matters worse for Foden, who missed out on the World Cup, it happened in front of Thomas Tuchel who names his England squad for the Nations League campaign on Friday.

It has been revealed that phil Foden is SENT OFF in the Manchester derby! 🟥 pic.twitter.com/sDkHoLMnjL.

In a recent development, and the goal? Initially it was ruled out for offside as Haaland superbly turned in Josko Gvardiol’s cross beyond the far post – he made that tricky finish look routine. But after a lengthy VAR check that decision was overturned by referee Michael Oliver.

Patrick Dorgu had played Haaland onside but the matter then was whether Fernández had touched the ball as he tried to reach the cross. He had not. But even if he had not, surely he was impeding Lisandro Martínez’s attempt to clear? He was certainly in the defender’s line of vision which fits the criteria for the offside to be given as it interfered with an opponent.

In a recent development, united can understandably complain but they can have no excuse. The pressure, already, will be beginning to mount on Carrick with just four points from four league games and down in 13th place. With a Carabao Cup tie at home to Brighton in midweek and a trip to Fulham next Sunday before the international break, he needs wins.

“We’ve only got 10 men,” goaded the City fans as the game headed into added time and United can expect to hear that again and again. And again.

Even so, at the death, Bryan Mbeumo – as otherwise anonymous as Matheus Cunha – had the chance to equalise after being shrewdly picked out by Fernandes. He was excellently thwarted by Gianluigi Donnarumma. But Mbeumo was clear inside the penalty area and had to score. Not that United would have deserved it. There were boos at the end and understandably so. United were just not good enough.

I’m confused. We put things in place in the game now. We have people in offices with all the screens for this decision. It’s more worrying about if that’s the interpretation of football now. If that’s the interpretation of not interfering in the game now, that’s really worrying for me. It’s a staggering explanation.

In a recent development, the decision isn’t going to change the season, but it’s had a major impact on the game. That decision wasn’t on us today. It’s up to us to create and score after that. We had moments. Of course it’s up to us to do that, but substantial moments in games like that have a big impact.

We did a lot of things well, it looked like we were growing well into the game. We looked dangerous. We’ll take the positives from the game today and move on well, but we’re not moving on lightly.

In a recent development, we could have created more. That’s an answer for us, but we could have. That’s our second defeat now, since I’ve been in charge, but we’re a good team and we’ll get back to wining ways.

The red card changed the blueprint of the game but credit to the players because the effort, spirit and togetherness has been brilliant.

According to recent reports, [On Foden’s red card] Can be a red card, but in the same action can be a red card for Bruno. It is what it is, we won.

In a recent development, changed the plan for us, and changed the plan for them. They are unbelievable in transition, and the moment we are with 10 men we give them no transitions.

When you are able to win a game with 10 players it’s fantastic, when this game is a derby it’s even better.

Last year with Chelsea I had a player sent off here after three minutes, this year 25, hopefully next time we play against 11vs11!

Industry observers note that we always knew it was going to be a tough game. What happened with Phil at the start wasn’t good for us, but we said at half-time it would make us feel better if we win and we’ve taken three points.

It just gives you more motivation to go on and get the points. It was really tough for us. We had to run more and fight more. We all shone, to a man, and we were brilliant.

Recent findings suggest that he was offside and what I can’t understand is it’s the rules... I went there because he was in front of him because that’s why Haaland was free at the back.

In a recent development, every season they come to our club and spend an hour and a half explaining the rules, and they seem so confident with that, and then you have five or six people making this mistake. It’s unacceptable.

We have to go home with this injustice.

Recent findings suggest that haaland speaking on Sky: “We had to go low which is not ideal, we like to keep the ball, to try to score goals but in these times you have to go a bit low and take your chances when possible. We managed to do that well and that demonstrates personality and character, to keep the ball away at Old Trafford with 10 men.”.

“We had to change the plan a bit, but Enzo gave us a plan where we could play to our different strengths and counter-attack a bit more. For me personally, I just had to be there, to try to wait for a chance, and if there’s a chance, I had to be ready to execute. We also needed fighters in the team, which we have plenty of. Look at our midfield - it’s something they like to do! I’m so, so proud of everyone.”.

Sources indicate that and on Donnarumma’s late save: “This wolf in goal giving you so much confidence, he looks a bit like a wolf. He is a mad man but he is a match-winner as well.”.

9 - Erling Haaland is now the top scorer in Premier League games between Manchester City and Manchester United:9 - Haaland (8 apps)8 - Agüero (13 apps)8 - Rooney (21 apps)Domination. pic.twitter.com/EBiifV12st.

City win the Old Trafford derby with 10 men and Enzo Maresca runs down the touchline to celebrate in front of the travelling fans while their players embrace Donnarumma after his late save.

There will be so much analysis of Foden’s red card, but more so how Haaland’s winner stood given the final result. Should Enzo Fernandez have been considered offside?

But if you are judging performances, City are worthy winners. They defended stoutly, carried a threat and kept the ball well for periods even though they were a man light. United were aimless and froze.

A mammoth victory, and one which perhaps puts the breaks on talk of an Arsenal procession.

In a recent development, what a chance for Mbeumo to equalise! Superb save by Donnarumma, after the United forward was found by a Bruno Fernandes disguised pass into the box. Mbeumo took the ball under his spell and shot with power, but the major goalkeeper pushed the shot over the bar.

United have a corner, but Michael Oliver blows for a foul, and that is surely that.

Martinez tries a straight ball towards Sesko, which is too high for the striker. United have perhaps just one more attack in them if they are too salvage a point.

Dalot with another poor cross that flies over everyone in the penalty area. Then Mainoo’s pass in midfield is intercepted by Anderson, and Ndiaye can bring the ball forward for City until he his tackled buy Martinez.

Fernandes drifts a cross behind for a City goal kick, between Sesko and Zirkzee and it looks like United are running out of time and ideas.

In a recent development, dorgu with another foul on Ndiaye, yet another break in play for City. And there are going to just FIVE minutes of added time, much to Old Trafford’s frustration.

In a recent development, haaland does well to bring City forward after another United attack breaks down, and Dorgu is penalised for a foul on Ndiaye. Another stoppage follows because the ball hits Michael Oliver. City can see the finish line so, and they would deserve their three points.

United have a corner after Guehi stands firm to block Cunha’s strike from distance. Maguire rises highest in the middle, but no United player gambled on the knockdown and his header drifts wide of the post.

Good work from Anderson against Mainoo in midfield, he receives a big cheer from the City fans. Carrick has thrown attackers on, but United have lost some structure and are not sustaining pressure.

Nico O’Reilly is now on for the closing stages, in place of Fernandez and Carrick has thrown on Zirkzee in place of Marcus Rashford. A United goal now would feel like a goal out of nowhere. City are playing the better football now and they have a corner.

United have lost all sense of momentum, City are keeping the ball for spells and then are happy for the game to be broken up stoppages.

Fernandez goes down looking for a penalty rather hopefully, and Maguire has been booked for his reaction as well as Fernandez for his role in the fracas. More and more time ticks away.

City are showing real resolve as well as quality here, Enzo Fernandez has just won a free-kick in the United half after a foul by Mainoo. The closest United have come in recent minutes was a glancing header wide from Mbeumo.

From that free-kick, Fernandez’s low delivery is close to being converted by Haaland or Guehi.

In a recent development, it’s a massive final 16 minutes here plus injuries for United. You’re at home to your derby rivals who have been down to 10 men since the 23rd minute and you’ve had just two players show up for the mostpart so far - Mainoo and Rashford. The rest are really going to have to lift it.

Fernandes stings the palms of Donnarumma with a strike from outside the box.

In a recent development, we have now had an explanation and evidence of why the goal stood. The VAR check for offside on Haaland found that he was in fact onside by fine margins, and that Fernandez (who was offside) did not affect Lisandro Martinez as he threw himself at a diving header (and missed). The Fernandez element feels the more debatable.

Sesko on for United. Surprised he’s not come on before. City fans singing “Enzo, he’s in your head, Enzo, Enzo” to the tune of the Cranberries’ Zombie – and then he goes and hits a post.

According to recent reports, what a final 30 minutes or so of football we have in store now. There will be an air of panic spreading through the United ranks, and Haaland, Ndiaye and Semenyo are still posing a threat.

Haaland and his City team-mates run off to celebrate in front of the away fans including Noel Gallagher.

It has been revealed that the goalscorer looked marginally ahead of Dorgu and offside, but the camera angles can deceive. The reasoning for the final decision is not entirely clear.

United fans were goading and laughing at their City counterparts when the goal was initially ruled out for offside but it’s City who have had the last laugh.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy.

It looks like they might be checking the position of Enzo Fernandez in the middle.

Industry observers note that haaland has the ball in the net but the flag is up for offside! Great finish at the back post from Gvardiol’s cross, but the City striker had just strayed offside. There is an ongoing VAR check, though.

City with a better sequence of passing but it does Ndiaye cannot get a shot away and then Fernandez commits another foul in midfield. Cunha with a poor cross behind for a City goal kick.

Bryan Mbeumo with a wild shot over the bar after cutting inside from the right, Mainoo was involved in propelling United forward once again. Then Cunha shoots over from a tight angle, but United are knocking on the door now.

According to recent reports, much better from United in the last few minutes, the crowd are engaged again and possibly for the first time in the game it feels like a goal might be coming. Nice idea from Rashford to let the ball run to Dorgu but the left-back is offside.

Industry observers note that kobbie Mainoo hits the post! Lovely strike from 25 yards after a Dalot pull-back is flicked into his path by Fernandes. Then United are back at the heart of the City defence, but Rashford’s shot deflects behind for a corner, from which the City goalkeeper is fouled.

Sources indicate that he’s been United’s best player by a distance so far this season and Kobbie Mainoo goes very close there to giving United the lead with a fine strike that hits the post. Next passage of play and he releases Rashford in on the left whose shot is pushed out for a corner.

Kobbie Mainoo was INCHES from opening the scoring against Manchester United 🤏 pic.twitter.com/l9v8mlxzk3.

In a recent development, haaland does well to win City a free-kick in the United half after rolling Martinez. City had an early United corner to defend but they did so well. Quite a slow tempo to the game all round.

In a recent development, fernandez’s deep delivery finds the unmarked Dias, and his header deflects behind for a City corner. Maguire heads away, and then Anderson’s cross drifts behind for a goal kick.

Strange moment as the game kicks-off while Sky’s Patrick Davison is still talking to Michael Carrick. He signs off in almost apologetic fashion for distracting the United manager from his job.

Ndiaye on for Cherki, so Maresca opting for a player who can dribble the ball over long distances.

Industry observers note that keane noted: “For me, Fernandes is the player who has been violent. I don’t think that is a red card for Foden. Foden is a bit daft, but so is Bruno.”.

A half that will be remembered for one thing and one thing only: Phil Foden’s red card for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes.

Sam Wallace was at Carrington this week to speak with Diogo Dalot, the Manchester United right-back who could make his 250th appearance for the club this afternoon. Dalot has been through some tumultuous times at Old Trafford, and is one of the great survivors in the squad. He talks about the scrutiny at United, his musical family and the negatives of social media for young players in an interview you can read here.

My sense is that while United fans generally understand and agree with the decision to stick with Carrick, they hope he is the long-term answer to get the club back to winning the Premier League or Champions League, while the rest of the world doubts it.

To most, it feels like Carrick remains an interim solution in all but name, entrusted with the keys to Old Trafford until a super coach can move in during the summer of 2027. Carrick will not see it that way, of course, but there are certain perceptions which will be tough to shake off.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the season’s first Manchester derby, with midfield rebuilds the theme of the summer on both sides of town.

Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez and Ayyoub Bouaddi could all be involved for City, who lost Rodri and Bernardo Silva in the engine room, while United have recruited Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos in an attempt to address a long-standing problem.

Sources indicate that rodri’s departure and a Community Shield shellacking by Arsenal prompted some gloomy forecasts for Enzo Maresca and City, but confidence has grown since. The late turnaround at home to Bournemouth on the opening weekend could well look very notable in a few months’ time, while Crystal Palace and Coventry have also been put away. Victory in Porto was probably Maresca’s most impressive result to date at City, though winning at Old Trafford would usurp that. Three points for City would mean they join Arsenal on a maximum of 12 points from four games.

Recent findings suggest that it has been a patchy start to the campaign for United and Michael Carrick, and this afternoon’s result will go a long way to shaping perceptions of where they are. The concession of a late equalise at Everton, in addition to a dreadful loss at Hull, adds a degree of pressure. United will be buoyed by their performance in this fixture in January, when they delivered possibly the best performance of the post-Ferguson years to slay City in a 2-0 win that could well have been four or five.

Industry observers note that with Tielemans, Bruno Fernandes and Kobbie Mainoo prominent in midfield, United are trying to shift to a more possession-heavy approach, but any success against City in recent times has tended to come on the counter-attack. Maresca’s team have had lots of the ball in their first few games of the season, so that is the expected pattern again.Full team news on the way later.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Peterborough United appointed Robbie Savage as their new manager on October 2nd, having been impressed by the work he'd done with Forest Green Rovers.
  • Savage is still juggling his life as a pundit and media personality, alongside the full-time gig with Peterborough in League One.
  • Naturally, there's been some opposition to that arrangement, and a run of seven games in all competitions without a win heading into this weekend isn't exactly helping his cause.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Peterborough United appointed Robbie Savage as their new manager on October 2nd, having been impressed by the work he'd done with Forest Green Rovers. His ex-Leicester City teammate, Emile Heskey, has now offered a peak behind the curtain to reveal exactly what the Posh boss is like.

Savage is still juggling his life as a pundit and media personality, alongside the full-time gig with Peterborough in League One.

Naturally, there's been some opposition to that arrangement, and a run of seven games in all competitions without a win heading into this weekend isn't exactly helping his cause.

Ironically, Savage's first game as Peterborough boss came against Leicester on October 10th, with his side racing into a 3-0 lead before seeing the game out to win 3-1, giving the former Fox the ideal start to life in the dugout.

After coming through at Man United and cutting his teeth with Crewe, it had been at Leicester where Savage had made a name for himself in the Premier League.

Heskey has been appearing on the 'Jamie Vardy's Having A Party' podcast, with the two former Leicester strikers trading stories from their time at the club.

In one part, Heskey is quizzed on any 'funny stories' he might have from his time at Filbert Street, where he responds to talk about Savage turning up in a purple Porsche, which Vardy finds easy to believe.

It has been revealed that vardy says: "Stuff like that brings the team together. He’s set himself up, but it’s good for the group.".

Heskey totally agrees, saying: "He was really good in taking it (the banter he got)," before revealing to a surprised Vardy: "He actually is quite sensitive and very insecure is Robbie.

"He’s one of those players where, before a game, we’d have to say, ‘We need you, Robbie, come on. You’re the best’.

Sources indicate that "He’d be nervous and like he didn’t want to play, pulling out of games. But this is this happy-go-lucky guy that you see all bubbly and that, but he is quite insecure.".

Heskey played with Savage at Leicester, before also linking up with him at Birmingham City later in the pair's careers.

As Heskey reveals, Savage was good at taking things on the chin when it came to the banter he got in the changing rooms. He was also pretty good at doing the same thing from rival fans as a player.

Savage finished his Leicester career with 204 appearances for the Foxes, along with 137 at Derby County, 100 at Blackburn Rovers and a further 88 for Birmingham. 346 of his career outings came in the Premier League, and you can tell by the tone of Heskey's voice that he picked up a fair bit of admiration for that.

Moving into coaching isn't easy, but Savage has had stints with Macclesfield and Forest Green, cutting his teeth at the bottom of the game to earn this chance at Peterborough.

It's a slightly different persona he will have to give off as a manager compared to a player, but every inch of his experience will be key to turning things around for Posh.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United are at the moment in the Premier League relegation zone after winning just one of their opening 10 league matches.

Their defensive record has been shambolic, and Pochettino needs to fix it as soon as possible. They have conceded 19 goals in the Premier League this season, the third fewest after Crystal Palace and Ipswich Town.

Their defensive struggles could encourage the Old Trafford board to invest in a fresh centre-back, with Newcastle’s Malick Thiaw emerging as a potential option.

Amid their defensive struggles, Manchester United are among several clubs keeping tabs on Malick Thiaw as they look to address their problems under latest manager, Mauricio Pochettino.

Newcastle United have set a massive € 80 million asking price for Malick Thiaw amid growing interest in the German international.

Sources indicate that several top European clubs have the 25-year-old centre-back on their radar after his impressive performances at St James’ Park. However, Newcastle are determined to not lose him on a cheap.

According to reports by Sky Germany, Matthias Jaissle’s side would want at least €80m for Thiaw, who remains under contract with the Magpies until 2029.

The German defender has also earned recognition from national team manager Jurgen Klopp, while Jaissle considers him an important part of his Newcastle side.

Newcastle signed the former Schalke defender from AC Milan in 2025 for a reported €35million.

Since arriving at St James’ Park, Thiaw has established himself as a key figure in the Magpies’ defence, making 64 appearances and contributing five goals and two assists.

His performances have attracted attention from several clubs, but Newcastle are in a strong position given his long-term contract.

Although a departure next summer has not been entirely ruled out, the Magpies are unlikely to entertain any approach that falls short of their €80million valuation.

In a recent development, manchester United have a clear gap to fill in their defence line. Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez haven’t eased the nerves this season and the Red Devils need a change at the back. Malick Thiaw can be the answer but he isn’t going to be cheap cost United heavy on their pockets.

The significant question isn’t the transfer value but whether he is the profile that Mauricio Pochettino needs when he rebuilds Manchester United.

By Matt Law | 19 Nov 2026 21:02, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 21:05.
