For each group of environmental variables, principal components were calculated and selected until the cumulative explained variance reached 80%; these components were used as predictors in the GDM. Colour shading denotes individual principal component dimensions. Variable loadings are shown in Extended Data Fig. 7. Model statistics and predictor importance using Monte Carlo sampling with 250 permutations are reported in Supplementary Tables 2 and 3. Landscape context is represented by the mean forest cover within a 200 m concentric buffer surrounding each plot.

Industry observers note that the three taxonomic groups with the strongest explanatory power—understorey plants, fungi and bacteria—also exhibited homogenization in the agricultural land uses (Fig. 2). This pattern suggests that homogenization is driven, to a large extent, by deterministic processes associated with land-use-induced changes in the environment, including direct impacts from soil disturbance and fertilization, and indirect effects from the deliberate replacement of forest species with a single, often non-native, target crop, and an alteration of vegetation structure by establishing even-aged structure. Additionally, biotic homogenization is driven by characteristics of the surrounding landscape (Supplementary Table 3). Processes leading to biotic differentiation can also emerge from changes in vegetation structure, as observed in most canopy-dwelling groups. Thus, for many groups, homogenization and differentiation can be linked to drastic changes in habitat structure following land-use intensification30 and in the remaining surrounding forests. Still, biotic differentiation can also be only weakly related to environmental conditions and the surrounding landscape, as for leaf litter spiders, mesostigmatid mites and springtails. Thus, biotic differentiation could be more stochastic and potentially driven by disturbance, legacy effects or meta-population and meta-community dynamics that were not quantified here.

Our results provide detailed insights into how tropical land-use intensification restructures biodiversity through concurrent changes in species richness and community composition. We document pronounced declines in γ- and α-multidiversity from lowland forests to monocultures, driven primarily by aboveground taxa. The diminishing tropical (degraded) forests and traditional agroforestry systems in our study region constitute irreplaceable reservoirs of biodiversity, but their biodiversity is in peril and requires urgent conservation and restoration actions. Divergent responses between aboveground and belowground compartments underscore the need to integrate multiple taxonomic groups spanning body size and mobility. We found no evidence for consistent community homogenization with land-use intensification. Instead, consistent with previous work, we found taxon-specific and seemingly idiosyncratic patterns of both biotic homogenization and differentiation19,20,22,50, but we also revealed a systematic shift from turnover to nestedness in monocultures. Our results call for careful interpretation of spatial patterns of community homogenization and differentiation, as well as long-term monitoring, because homogenization–differentiation trends can be scale-dependent (in line with the landscape divergence hypothesis) and can differ between smallholder and industrial plantations, which are not included in our study. In addition, early stages of assemblage simplification may mask trajectories towards biotic homogenization. Overall, our results demonstrate that land-use intensification alters multidiversity across spatial scales, with ecosystem-wide consequences for biotic communities and their abiotic environment, and suggest that habitat filtering has a stronger role than neutral or dispersal processes. Effective conservation will benefit from recognizing the conservation value of traditional agricultural systems, which, in our study region, buffer the loss of multiple generalist forest species and exhibit high levels of β-diversity. These traditional agricultural systems are currently under pressure from conversion and lie outside the conservation focus and landscape planning. Furthermore, implementing sustainable management practices2,3,4 within conventional monocultures could help mitigate biodiversity losses and promote landscape differentiation in these agricultural landscapes. Differentiation across multiple taxonomic groups should not overshadow the homogenization occurring within key taxonomic groups such as bats, birds, trees and understorey plants. Therefore, there is a growing need to establish conservation priorities for focal taxonomic groups, including tailored landscape-scale solutions to maximize the γ-diversity of forest-associated biodiversity, such as conserving irreplaceable endemic species in this biodiversity hotspot.

Our study was conducted in the province of Jambi on the island of Sumatra, Indonesia. This tropical lowland region has undergone extensive land-use changes since the twentieth century and is a showcase of smallholder agriculture in Indonesia13,42. Two sample landscapes, ‘Harapan’ and ‘Bukit Duabelas’ (with loam and clay Acrisol soils, respectively), were selected within Jambi Province. In each landscape, four 50 m × 50 m replicate plots were established in each of the four land-use types common to the region: primary degraded forest (sensu ref. 51), jungle rubber (a traditional agroforestry system established by planting rubber trees inside secondary forest), smallholder monoculture rubber plantation, and smallholder monoculture oil palm plantation—totalling 32 plots. The number of replicate sites per land use is comparable to that of other ecological studies in tropical lowland regions52. Various measurements, such as microclimate, were taken at the plot level. Other measurements, such as most biodiversity sampling, were taken in five permanent 5 m × 5 m subplots established within each plot. All sites were selected in 2012. At this time, rubber plantations were established 7–16 years ago, and oil palm plantations were established 8–15 years ago. For jungle rubber, plots selected contained older non-rubber trees, with individual rubber trees of varying ages not planted in rows13.

According to recent reports, jungle rubber, rubber and oil palm plots were owned and managed by smallholder farmers, whereas the forest plots were located in the Bukit Duabelas National Park and the Harapan Rainforest Restoration concession area (PT REKI). In our study region, smallholders generally do not cultivate food crops alongside the target cash crops examined here, with only a few exceptions8,42,43. Our study’s oil palm plots were on average surrounded by ~13.6% forest and ~61% oil palm plantations within 1 km buffers compared with ~0.45% and ~96% in industrial oil palm plantations, respectively41. Further, our oil palm plots received less herbicide (0.73 l ha−1 year−1) and fertilizer (6.6 kg N ha−1 year−1) compared with industrial oil palm plantations41 (1.12 l ha−1 year−1 and 141 kg N ha−1 year−1). Rubber and oil palm smallholder plantations represent the highest land-use intensity level among the systems included in our study. Yet land-use intensity is even higher in large-scale industrial plantations. More information on the study region, study design, land-use types and management practices of the smallholder systems is provided elsewhere8,13,42. Data compilation in these studies has also served as a basis for our study, but has been substantially expanded in recent years. For example, a multi-taxon perspective was offered in ref. 42 for 3 taxonomic groups, in ref. 13 for 9 taxonomic groups, and in ref. 8 for 14 taxonomic groups.

We studied 24 different biodiversity indicators distributed from the canopy to the soil, namely: (1) ants (Hymenoptera: Formicidae), (2) beetles (Coleoptera), (3) true bugs (Hemiptera), (4) flies (Diptera)53, (5) parasitoids (parasitoid Hymenoptera), (6) spiders (Araneae), and (7) springtails (Collembola), from the canopy; (8) bats (Chiroptera), (9) birds (Aves), (10) butterflies (Lepidoptera), (11) trees (Tracheophyta), (12) understorey plants (Tracheophyta), (13) spiders, (14) beetles, and (15) ants, from the leaf litter; (16) centipedes (Chilopoda), (17) springtails, (18) mesostigmatid mites (Mesostigmata), and (19) oribatid mites (Oribatida), from the litter and soil; and (20) fungi, (21) testate amoebae, (22) protists, (23) bacteria, and (24) archaea, from the soil (Supplementary Table 4). These biodiversity indicators represent a wide spectrum of taxa, encompassing all domains of life, various trophic levels, and diverse ecological strategies, dispersal abilities and body sizes. This comprehensive dataset builds on a long-term collaborative effort that generated detailed insights into individual taxonomic groups, including species descriptions54,55,56,57,58,59, field guides60,61,62,63 and functional and trophic interactions53,64,65,66—as well as ecosystem-wide analyses and integrative studies linking ecological and socio-economic dimensions8,13,42.

It has been revealed that canopy arthropods (ants, beetles, bugs, flies, parasitoids, spiders and springtails) were collected by canopy fogging in the dry season from May to October 2013. In each of the 32 plots, 3 representative canopy locations were selected, avoiding canopy gaps and overly dense canopies. At each of the 3 locations, 16 rectangular traps (1 m × 1 m) fitted with 100 ml ethanol-filled bottles were suspended from ropes beneath the selected canopies at approximately 1.50 m. 50 ml of DECIS EC 25 (active ingredient: deltamethrine 25 g l−1), dissolved in 4 l of petroleum white oil, was applied to the target canopies from the ground using the Swingtec Swingfog SN 50. In all four land-use systems, target canopies consisted of leaves from different trees. Stunned and dead arthropods were collected from the traps up to 2 h after the complete application of the fogging mixture. Canopy fogging was conducted in the early morning, immediately after sunrise, to minimize air movement that would disperse the fog. This was done only in dry conditions, ensuring that small arthropods would not become trapped in water droplets on leaves and branches. Overall, 372,146 canopy arthropod individuals were collected this way53 and sorted into morphospecies for selected taxa. This study includes data from the following taxa: ants (Hymenoptera: Formicidae) 179 morphospecies67; beetles (Coleoptera) 397 morphospecies in 4 families (Chrysomelidae, Curculionidae, Elateridae and Staphylinidae)68; true bugs (Hemiptera) 301 morphospecies in 2 suborders (Auchenorrhyncha and Heteroptera); flies (Diptera) 483 morphospecies in 2 suborders (Brachycera and Nematocera, including Eudiptera)69; parasitoid wasps (Hymenoptera: “Parasitica”) 1,012 morphospecies in 6 families (Braconidae, Ceraphronidae, Encyrtidae, Eulophidae, Scelionidae and Platygastridae)70; spiders (Araneae) 445 morphospecies71; and springtails (Collembola) 60 morphospecies72. Recorded (morpho-)species across taxa are deposited in the http://ecotaxonomy.org database and in refs. 60,61,62.

Sources indicate that bats were surveyed using mist nets and harp traps between April and August 2015. We used telescopic aluminium poles to install mist nets with a total length of 48 m, as well as two harp traps (1.35 m × 1.75 m) in presumed bat flyways. Mist nets were 3 m high, with a 19-mm mesh size, and were installed at ground level or up to 3 m high, depending on plot conditions. Each plot was sampled from 17:30 to 22:00 on two consecutive nights, resulting in an average sampling effort of 1,296 m2 of mist net hours. We checked the nets and traps every 15 min until 20:00 and every 30 min thereafter. Harp traps were left on site until and checked the morning after. Captured bats were left in tissue pouches until the nets were closed. Then bat morphology was measured to identify them according to the latest bat species checklist for Sumatra73. We tagged the bats’ nails with nail polish colour codes to identify recaptures and released them afterwards. This study includes data from 20 bat species. In plot HJ3, no individuals were caught (total abundance = 0).

Birds were sampled with point counts74, as well as automated sound recordings, from May to July 2013. Point counts and automated sound recordings lasted 20 min and were conducted from the centre of each plot between 6:00 and 10:00. The timing of point counts alternated between early and late morning, and all plots were visited three times. The automated sound recorders (SM2+ with two SMX-II microphones, Wildlife Acoustics) were set up at ~2 m height to record at a 44.1 kHz sampling rate in stereo, simultaneously across land-use types; one recording, starting at sunrise, was used for each plot. Point count detections of individuals flying above the canopy were excluded, and unfamiliar bird calls were recorded using a Sennheiser ME-66 directional microphone. The automated sound recordings were uploaded to ecoSound-web, an online platform for ecoacoustics75, for two independent ornithologists to identify all bird calls within an estimated 35 m radius. Only bird species identified by both ornithologists in recordings of each plot were used and subsequently merged with the species list obtained from the point counts. Aural detections were confirmed with cross-checks on the Xeno-Canto online bird call database (https://xeno-canto.org/). This study encompasses data from 114 bird species. For birds, BO1_5 data were unavailable. Therefore, when analyses required non-missing values, imputation was performed by using the average from plots of the same land use within the same landscape (that is, Bukit). However, γ-diversity values for birds may be underestimated.

Recent findings suggest that butterflies (Lepidoptera: Papilionidae, Pieridae, Lycaneidae and Nymphalidae) were recorded from all 32 study plots in the dry season of 2017 between August and October. Butterflies were collected using sweep netting on three parallel 50-m transects per plot, with two transects on the outer boundaries and the third through the centre. Sweep netting was conducted once in the morning (8:00−11:00) and repeated in the afternoon (13:00−16:00). Except for two voucher specimens per collected species, all butterfly individuals were released on the evening of the sampling day. This study includes data based on butterfly specimens from 219 species76. Recorded morphospecies are deposited in the http://ecotaxonomy.org database and in ref. 63.

Sources indicate that plant inventories were conducted between February 2013 and August 2014, using different sampling schemes for large trees and vascular understorey plants30. All trees per plot with a diameter of ≥10 cm at a height of 1.3 m were identified. Vascular understorey plants were censused in the five 5 m × 5 m subplots per plot, including all plant individuals, such as terrestrial plants (herbs, shrubs, climbers and juvenile trees) and epiphytes growing up to 3 m above the ground. 281 tree species were present in both censuses (for large trees and understorey plants). To avoid inflating species richness, they were retained only in the matrix that included large trees. Species identification was conducted in the field if possible or otherwise based on field photographs and herbarium specimens deposited at BIOT, BO, GOET, and the herbaria at Jambi University and Harapan Rainforest (acronyms follow Index Herbarium: http://sweetgum.nybg.org/science/ih/). The number of all individuals per species and plot was used for analyses. In total, this study includes 443 tree species and 976 vascular plant species in the understorey.

Leaf litter was collected from three of the five subplots within each of the study plots. In each subplot, leaf litter from 1 m2 of ground was sieved using a coarse mesh (width of 2 cm). All macro-invertebrates visible to the naked eye were hand-collected from the sieved samples, stored in 65% ethanol and transported to the laboratory for identification12. Recorded (morpho-)species are deposited in the http://ecotaxonomy.org database. This study includes data on 135 morphospecies of ants, 170 morphospecies of beetles, and spider specimens from 132 morphospecies. For leaf litter spiders and leaf litter beetles, no individuals were detected in plots HO2 and BO4, respectively (total abundance = 0).

Sources indicate that between October and November 2013, random samples were taken from three 5 m × 5 m subplots per plot (a total of 96 samples). Samples were taken at least 2 m from the next tree or dead-wood accumulation. Each sample measured 16 cm × 16 cm and included the complete litter layer and the underlying topsoil to a depth of 5 cm, obtained using a spade. Animals were extracted using heat and stored in 70% ethanol77. This study includes data from 12 morphospecies. In plot BR2, no individuals were detected (total abundance = 0).

Samples were taken in October 2013. In each plot, one randomly positioned soil core (16 cm × 16 cm) was taken to a depth of 5 cm in the mineral soil. Litter and soil layers were separated in the field and extracted independently. Animals were extracted by heat for 5–10 days until the substrate was completely dry78, collected in dimethyleneglycol–water solution (1:1) and stored in 70% ethanol79. This study includes data from 58 morphospecies.

Three soil cores were taken in October and November 2013 from each of 32 plots. Soil cores (16 cm × 16 cm) were collected from the litter layer and the underlying soil to a depth of 5 cm. Animals were extracted under a heat gradient78, collected in dimethyleneglycol–water solution (1:1) and thereafter stored in 70% ethanol. Identification of soil mites was done on microscopic slides to (morpho)species level. Recorded (morpho)species are deposited in the http://ecotaxonomy.org database. More details are described in ref. 80. This study includes data from 110 morphospecies of mesostigmatid mites and 219 morphospecies of oribatid mites.

Soil samples were collected in October and November 2016. In three subplots (5 m × 5 m) per plot, five soil cores (15 cm depth, 4 cm diameter) were taken and pooled, yielding a total of three samples per plot. Samples were sieved (50 × 50 mm mesh) and freeze-dried. DNA extraction, sequencing, and assignment of OTUs have been described81. Data have been deposited in the Dryad repository82. This study includes data from 12,309 OTUs.

It has been revealed that litter and upper mineral soil samples (to a depth of 50 mm) were collected in October and November 2013 using a 50 mm diameter corer. Testate amoebae were extracted from the samples by washing 1 g dry weight sample through a 500-µm mesh and back-sieving the filtrate through a 10-µm mesh. More details are described in ref. 83. This study includes data from 190 morphospecies of testate amoebae.

In a recent development, soil samples were collected from each study plot and processed (sieving, freeze-drying and milling) to extract DNA for protist community analysis84. This study includes data from 5,204 OTUs of protists.

Soil samples were taken at the subplot level, DNA was extracted and amplicons were generated with primer pairs targeting the 16S ribosomal RNA gene of bacteria and archaea and used to assess bacterial and archaeal community compositions separately33. This study includes data on 16,413 bacterial OTUs and 448 archaeal amplicon sequence variants. For archaea, HF3 data were unavailable. Therefore, when analyses required non-missing values, imputation was performed by using the average from plots with the same land use within the same landscape (that is, Harapan). However, γ-diversity values for archaea may be underestimated.

We consider 24 environmental variables distributed into 4 groups: microclimate, vegetation, litter and soil (Supplementary Table 5).

Sources indicate that meteorological stations were set up in the centre of each plot to measure hourly below-canopy air temperature and relative humidity at 2 m height between June 2013 and October 2014. Additionally, soil sensors were used to measure soil temperature and moisture at a depth of 0.3 m (ref. 85).

Different aspects of structural complexity have been measured using terrestrial laser scanning in each of the 32 plots in September and October 2016. Based on a single-scan approach, we calculated the effective number of layers, which quantifies vertical stratification86, and the stand structural complexity index87, which describes the complexity of vegetation’s three-dimensional occupation of space. We collected nine single scans, evenly distributed across each plot, and aggregated at the plot level using mean and standard deviation, the latter describing the spatial heterogeneity of vegetation structure88. Additionally, hemispherical photographs were taken at 1.2 m above the ground from 32 positions within each plot to derive canopy openness42. Fine root production was estimated by installing 16 ingrowth cores per plot8.

It has been revealed that aboveground litterfall was assessed by placing 16 litter traps (75 cm × 75 cm) in each plot. Traps were emptied monthly from March 2013 to April 2014. For oil palms, pruned leaves were counted, and a subsample was dried and weighed. For litter nutrients, aliquots of material from the litter–fermentation layer of all 32 plots were dried at 65 °C for 72 h, milled, and analysed for total C and N concentrations using an elemental analyser89 (Carlo Erba Instruments).

Recent findings suggest that soil sampling was conducted in 2013. Within a 50 m × 50 m area at each site, ten grid points were selected (including the five subplots), and soil samples were taken from the top 0–0.1 m depth. The ten subplots were averaged to represent each site. Soil biochemical characteristics (that is, pH, soil organic carbon (kg C m−2), total nitrogen (g N m−2), 15N natural abundance signatures (‰ 15N), effective cation exchange capacity (ECEC; mmolc m−2), base saturation (%), aluminium saturation (%) and extractable phosphorus (g P m−2)) were determined on air-dried and sieved (2 mm) soil samples. Organic carbon and total nitrogen were analysed using a CN analyser (Vario EL Cube, Elementar Analysis Systems) and 15N by isotope ratio mass spectrometry (Delta Plus, Finnigan MAT). ECEC was determined by percolating the soils with unbuffered 1 mol l−1 NH4Cl, and cations (Ca, Mg, K, Na, Al, Fe and Mn) were measured in percolates using an inductively coupled plasma-atomic emission spectrometer (iCAP 6300 Duo VIEW ICP Spectrometer, Thermo Fisher Scientific). Base and aluminium saturation were calculated as percentage exchangeable bases or aluminium on the ECEC. Extractable phosphorus was determined using the Bray 2 method for acidic tropical soils. Soil physical characteristics for each site included bulk density (g cm−3; core method)32,90. Soil respiration was measured monthly in 2013 using a chamber located on four subplots per plot. Gas samples were analysed using a gas chromatograph with an electron capture detector and a flame ionization detector (GC 6000 Vega Series2, Carlo Erba Instruments)91.

Recent findings suggest that species matrices. Species observations taken at the subplot level were aggregated into plot-level observations.

According to recent reports, environmental data. We conducted a principal component analysis for each group of variables, with variables transformed (when needed) and scaled. We selected the first components until the cumulative explained variance reached 80%. Variable contributions of these selected principal components are displayed in Extended Data Fig. 7.

Landscape data. We calculated landscape metrics within 200 m buffers around our plot centres using a manually classified land-use map derived from satellite imagery from 2016 (ref. 92). We used the R package landscapemetrics93 to calculate the mean forest coverage.

Species occurrences were calculated separately for each taxonomic group.

α- and γ-diversities. We quantified diversity using the Hill number framework, expressing it as effective species numbers, where q0 disregards species abundances and is therefore more sensitive to rare species (species richness) and q1 weights species in proportion to their abundances, favouring neither rare nor dominant species (that is, effective number of common species; Shannon diversity)94. In addition, we calculated rarefaction–extrapolation curves for the 24 taxonomy groups at plot (that is, α-diversity; Supplementary Figs. 1 and 2) and each land use (that is, γ-diversity; Supplementary Fig. 3) level using the iNEXT R package95,96.

α- and γ-multidiversity. To assess the multidiversity across all 24 taxonomic groups, first, we normalized the observed effective number of species at the plot or land-use type level using the min–max scaling approach, following: y = (x − min(x))/(max(x) − min(x)), where x is the set of observed effective number of species. The normalized effective number of species (y) ranges between 0 and 1, with 0 referring to the lowest observed value and 1 to the highest observed value for each taxonomic group across plots or land uses. This method ensures equal weight for all taxonomic groups, despite differences in their diversity ranges, and is a common approach in multi-taxon studies1,97. To obtain a single α-diversity index, we averaged the normalized values—that is, the overall diversity across all taxonomic groups at the plot level (α-multidiversity). For γ-multidiversity, we likewise averaged the normalized values—that is, based on the lowest and highest observed diversity values at the land-use types. In addition, we calculated α- and γ-multidiversity separately for aboveground and belowground taxonomy groups.

Sources indicate that β-Diversity and β-multidiversity. For each taxonomic group, we calculated β-diversity using pairwise dissimilarity matrices (presence–absence data; index family = jaccard; Supplementary Fig. 7). The Jaccard pairwise dissimilarity (βjacc, total β-diversity) among plots was computed as βjacc = βjtu + βjne, where βjtu accounted for turnover and βjne accounted for the nestedness (measured as the nestedness-resultant dissimilarity fraction of Jaccard dissimilarity), measured on a normalized scale from 0 to 1. Calculations were performed using the beta.pair from the package betapart v1.6. Mathematically, in cases of complete biodiversity loss—that is, zero individuals detected—plots have a total β-diversity of one as they do not share species with other plots; in these cases, we assumed turnover to be 0 and nestedness to be 1, considering that β-diversity result from species losses; this was implemented manually as it is not included in the output of betapart98,99. We also calculated β-diversity using Sørensen and its components and the abundance-based indices Bray–Curtis (weights absolute differences in abundance equally, so that abundant species contribute most to dissimilatiry)100 and Morisita–Horn (weighted towards common and dominant species and it is robust to sample size)101. These abundance-based dissimilarity indices were calculated using the vegan R package102 (Bray–Curtis: method = “bray”, binary = F; and Morisita–Horn dissimilarity: method = “horn”, binary = F; Supplementary Fig. 8). For Morisita–Horn, it is not possible to calculate dissimilarity when communities have zero abundance. Therefore, for Morisita–Horn, plots with at least one taxon for which the abundance was zero were excluded (BO4, BR2, HJ3, HO2 and HR4). We aggregated the pairwise dissimilarities to a mean pairwise dissimilarity for each taxonomic group for each plot (n = 32 plots for 24 taxonomic groups). To calculate β-multidiversity, we normalized the aggregated pairwise dissimilarity at the plot level using the min–max scaling approach1,97, as y = (x − min(x))/(max(x) − min(x)), where x is the set of pairwise dissimilarity at plot level. The normalized pairwise dissimilarity (y) ranges between 0 and 1, with 0 referring to the lowest observed value and 1 to the highest observed value for each taxonomic group across plots. We average the normalized β-diversity values across taxonomic groups at the plot level (either including all taxonomic groups or only aboveground and belowground taxonomic groups).

We used the ANOVA type II test to assess the influence of land use on α- and β-multidiversity. In addition, we used ANOVA type III to evaluate the influence of land use, compartment (aboveground and belowground), and their interaction. This analysis was implemented in the car package103. We checked for normality and homogeneity of variance of residuals using the Shapiro–Wilk test and Levene’s test for homogeneity of variance. Further, we tested statistical pairwise differences using multiple comparisons of means with Tukey, with P values adjusted with the false discovery rate—that is, the expected proportion of false discoveries amongst the rejected hypotheses104—using the p.adjust function (fdr) in the stats R package.

For each taxon, we determined significant differences in diversity (α or β) of the current land use compared with the forest by calculating log ratio and 95% adjusted bootstrap confidence intervals as follows:.

where ‘agricultural land use’ is the diversity value in the agricultural land use and ‘\(\overline{\mathrm{forest}}\)’ is the mean of the diversity in the forest. Negative and positive values indicate decreases and increases in diversity compared to the forest, respectively. For α-diversity, a pseudocount of 1 was added to all species count values to handle zeros while symmetrically preserving relative differences for count-like data—that is, \(\log [({\rm{a}}{\rm{g}}{\rm{r}}{\rm{i}}{\rm{c}}{\rm{u}}{\rm{l}}{\rm{t}}{\rm{u}}{\rm{r}}{\rm{a}}{\rm{l}}\,{\rm{l}}{\rm{a}}{\rm{n}}{\rm{d}}\,{\rm{u}}{\rm{s}}{\rm{e}}+1)/(\bar{{\rm{f}}{\rm{o}}{\rm{r}}{\rm{e}}{\rm{s}}{\rm{t}}}+1)]\). In the case of turnover and nestedness (0–1-scaled data), zeros were handled by adding 50% of the minimum non-zero value prior to log ratio calculation105, specifically, a pseudocount of 0.0357 was added for turnover (minimum non-zero value = 0.0714) and 0.00256 was added for nestedness (minimum non-zero value = 0.0051). We then calculated 95% confidence intervals for the log ratio using 10,000 bootstrap replicates (R package boot106, adjusted percentile bootstrap (bca-type)). If the 95% confidence intervals did not include zero, this indicated a significant difference between land use and the forest. As the results for diversity changes were largely consistent across q0 and q1 (Supplementary Fig. 9), we only show the results for q0. In addition, we performed t-tests to assess for significant differences between the log ratio and zero (forests as a reference), adjusting the P values using the false discovery rate (Supplementary Results).

Industry observers note that we calculated Pearson’s correlation with false discovery rate correction for species richness and pairwise Jaccard dissimilarity indices between each taxonomic group, irrespective of land-use type. The correlations are displayed in Supplementary Fig. 5.

In a recent development, dissimilarities between pairwise observations were calculated separately for each taxonomic group and land use. Pairwise Jaccard dissimilarity was calculated using vegdist function (method = jaccard and binary = TRUE) in the R package vegan102,107. Afterward, we calculated mean pairwise dissimilarities for each site combination across all taxa. We then visualized the patterns in community composition using a non-metric multidimensional scaling (NMDS) analysis of the mean pairwise dissimilarities for each plot combination. We used the envfit function from the R package vegan102,107 to fit environmental vectors onto the ordination of dissimilarities. The resulting plot coordinates on the NMDS scale were grouped by land-use type. In addition, significant differences among land uses were tested using an analysis of similarities (ANOSIM) on the pairwise Jaccard dissimilarity matrix using the ANOSIM function (permutations = 9999) from the R package vegan102,107. To test whether land use had an effect at the ecosystem level, including biotic and abiotic variables, we ran a multiple factor analysis. This analysis enables the identification of a common structure across two or more data matrices without assuming causation44, with canonical ordination methods being among the most powerful approaches for testing ecological relationships in a multivariate context44. To quantify the overall similarity (matrix correlation) between taxonomic groups in the multiple factor analysis, we used the RV coefficient, where 0 indicates no similarity and 1 indicates perfect similarity (Supplementary Table 1). We implemented this additional metric to test the robustness of our conclusions.

It has been revealed that A GDM model was applied to each taxonomic group. We used the respective species matrix, the selected principal components for each group of environmental variables (see the section ‘Environmental data’), and the geographic plot coordinates to run the model. The execution of the GDM was performed using the gdm R package108. The contributions of environmental variables (principal components; Extended Data Fig. 7) and distance were estimated by extracting the maximum spline values (Supplementary Table 3). Significance testing of variables was performed using Monte Carlo sampling, implemented in the gdm.varImp function, with 250 permutations (Supplementary Table 2). All the analyses were performed in R v4.5.1 (ref. 109).

Industry observers note that venn diagrams include aboveground taxonomic groups together or each group separately. They illustrate the shared and unique species, along with their percentages, across land-use types (i.e., γ-diversity). Land-use types are: forest (F), jungle rubber (J), rubber plantation (R), and oil palm plantation (O).

In a recent development, venn diagrams include aboveground taxonomic groups together or each group separately. They illustrate the shared and unique species numbers and percentages across land-use types (i.e., γ-diversity). Land-use types are: forest (F), jungle rubber (J), rubber plantation (R), and oil palm plantation (O).

Industry observers note that multidiversity across scales was calculated using standardized values (min-max scaling approach). For α-, and β-multidiversity, significant differences tested using two-sided ANOVA Type III. Linear model fits using ggeffect (marginal mean and confidence intervals, n = 32 plots). For γ-multidiversity aboveground, values shifted from 0.99, 0.72, 0.18, and 0.07 in forest, jungle rubber, rubber and oil palm plantations, while γ-multidiversity belowground, values shifted from 0.74, 0.73, 0.21, and 0.51 in forest, jungle rubber, rubber and oil palm plantations, respectively. For α-multidiversity aboveground, values shifted from 0.64 (95% CIs: 0.58 − 0.70), 0.47 (0.41 − 0.53), 0.24 (0.18 − 0.30), and 0.22 (0.16 − 0.28) in forest, jungle rubber, rubber, and oil palm plantations, while α-multidiversity belowground, values shifted from 0.50 (0.44− 0.56), 0.48 (0.42 − 0.54), 0.32 (0.26 − 0.38), and 0.41 (0.35 − 0.47) in forest, jungle rubber, rubber and oil palm plantations, respectively (n = 32 plots). For β-multidiversity aboveground, values varied from 0.42 (0.37 − 0.47), 0.52 (0.47−0.57), 0.54 (0.49−0.59), 0.49 (0.44− 0.54) in forest, jungle rubber, rubber and oil palm plantations, respectively, while β-multidiversity belowground, values were consistent across land uses ~0.45.

Pearson correlations calculated using stats and correlations plotted using ggscatter (mean and confidence intervals; n = 8 plots for land-use type).

It has been revealed that points and lines (mean and 95% confidence intervals using 10,000 bootstrap replicates) represent log ratio in diversity associated with land-use intensification using forests as a control. CIs not overlapping zero indicate differences from the forest (coloured points; black CIs; shaded when the 95% CIs include zero). Negative and positive values indicate decreases or increases in turnover or nestedness, respectively, relative to mean forest values.

Environmental groups include litter (cumulative percentage of variance = 86%), microclimate (cumulative percentage of variance = 90%), soil (cumulative percentage of variance = 84%), and vegetation (cumulative percentage of variance = 84%). Variables and abbreviations are explained in Supplementary Table 5. For each variable group, dimensions were selected until 80% of the explained variance was reached. Colour shades indicate the selected dimensions of the principal component analyses, with the darkest shades representing the first dimension and lighter shades representing higher dimensions (up to dimension four in the soil group).

Supplementary Results, Supplementary Figs. 1–10, Supplementary Tables 1–5 and Supplementary references.

Multiple comparisons using t-test to assess significant differences between the log ratio and zero (forests as a reference), adjusting the P values using the false discovery rate.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sam Varley | 19 Nov 2026 23:57.

Aiming to build a lead at the top of the League One table on the return from the international break, Huddersfield Town will welcome Leicester City to the Accu Stadium on Saturday.

The hosts presently lead second-placed Stockport County on goal difference while their visitors sit 11th and four points off the top six.

Huddersfield Town return from the November international break on Saturday aiming to pick up where they left off and pull clear at the top of the League One table.

Aiming to kick on from two disappointing years in England's third tier and fight for promotion back to the Championship, following the permanent appointment of Martin Drury over the summer, they have enjoyed an impressive campaign thus far, currently sitting top having earned 29 points from their first 14 games, winning eight and only losing one of those.

That solitary defeat came in mid-September, and the Terriers have won five and drawn two of seven league outings since, having taken on Luton Town in their final game before the break on the back of four straight victories over Plymouth Argyle, Peterborough United, Wigan Athletic and Bradford City, scoring 11 goals and conceding just two across those.

Drury's men had to settle for a point, though, levelling early in the second half through Joe Taylor in a 1-1 draw before heading into a pair of cup games, firstly bowing out of the FA Cup to fourth-tier Exeter City.

They would then beat Liverpool Under-21s 4-0 in the EFL Trophy last weekend, and now with their full focus back on League One, currently ahead of Stockport County on goal difference and third-placed Oxford United by three points, Huddersfield Town will hope to continue their hot streak and put another victory on the board.

Their visitors, meanwhile, return from the break with their sights set on the playoff places and the hopes of continuing an improved run of their own.

After suffering back-to-back defeats from the Premier League to League One, and turning to Russell Martin in the summer, Leicester City endured another poor start, managing just two wins and nine in their first eight games.

The Foxes appear to have turned a corner since, though, putting three more wins and a draw on the board in their last five league outings to climb into the top half, having beaten Doncaster Rovers, Bromley and Wigan Athletic alongside an away loss to Luton Town.

Martin's men then hosted Stevenage in their final league game before the break and had to settle for a point, having twice led through Sammy Braybrooke and Kamari Doyle and been pegged back, before they recorded consecutive cup victories, getting the better of Oxford City in the FA Cup and Walsall in the EFL Trophy.

Now also focused back on their League One bid, having moved within four points of the playoff spots and five of fourth place, Leicester City will hope to get back to winning ways with the scalp of the league leaders to move closer to the frontrunners on Saturday.

Huddersfield Town will remain without injured defenders Jack Whatmough and Murray Wallace and midfielders Marcus McGuane and Herbie Kane.

Drury fielded a strong team for their EFL Trophy game last week, with star forward Joe Taylor scoring another two goals to go alongside his 10 for the season in League One, and he will continue to spearhead the attack.

Derensili Sanches Fernandes will return to join him after international duty with Cape Verde, having also shone this season with seven goals and six assists in 14 League One appearances.

Leicester City have a relatively clean bill of health, other than long-term injuries for goalkeeper Jakub Stolarczyk and defender Ben Nelson.

Martin found a somewhat settle starting XI for the most part before the break, and Warren O'Hora, Harry Souttar and Caleb Okoli are bound to continue in a back three with Will Alves and Luke Thomas operating as full-backs.

Will Smallbone, John Lundstram and 18-year-old prospect Louis Page are likely left to compete for two midfield spots, while Sammy Braybrooke and Kamari Doyle may again support front man Emil Riis, who has scored six goals in nine league games so far this term, despite competition from Liam Cullen, Wes Burns and Conor Chaplin.

Huddersfield Town possible starting lineup:.

Young; Balker, Bowat, Roughan; Bronkhorst, Humphreys, Collins, Mumba; Sanches Fernandes, Taylor, Fletcher.

Leicester City possible starting lineup:.

McCarthy; O'Hora, Souttar, Okoli; Alves, Lundstram, Page, Thomas; Braybrooke, Riis, Doyle.

Leicester City certainly appear to be improving and showing their class more after a tough start, but they face a tough test away at a formidable Huddersfield Town team who also boast an abundance of quality and have settled into life under Drury perfectly.

With Taylor and Sanches Fernandes both in hot streaks, we fancy the Terriers to come out on top at home in a high-quality encounter.

  • The Blues winger had in fact scored in the game, netting his side's second goal at the Cardiff City Stadium, but saw his game fall apart in the second-half.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 17:34 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 17:49 EST, 17 November 2026.

Chelsea star Pedro Neto lost his cool while playing for Portugal in their win over Wales as he received two yellow cards in as many minutes before clashing with opposing manager Craig Bellamy.

The Blues winger had in fact scored in the game, netting his side's second goal at the Cardiff City Stadium, but saw his game fall apart in the second-half.

He was first booked for a high challenge on the back of Brennan Johnson's leg – a tackle which some may argue could have been a red in itself.

One minute and 59 seconds later, he was shown his second yellow when he slid in on Johnson again. He didn't appear to make too much contact, if any, but left the Wales man sprawling to avoid it.

German referee Sven Jablonski demonstrated no hesitation in sending Neto off, but the winger wasn't going to take it lying down.

He had to be held back by captain Bruno Fernandes as he tried to confront Johnson, and seemingly managed to shout in his direction before reluctantly making his way off the field.

Pedro Neto was sent off while playing for Portugal against Wales after two yellow cards in under two minutes.

He also had a confrontation with Wales manager Craig Bellamy (right) as he left the field of play.

Before that, though, he had a conversation with Wales boss Craig Bellamy, with officials initially trying to separate the two, with Neto looking angry.

Bellamy, though, spoke to Neto and embraced him before finally walking down the tunnel.

The 26-year-old will now serve a one-game suspension, meaning he will miss the first leg of Portugal's Nations League quarter-final, which will be played in March.

Jorge Jesus's side secured top spot in their group with the win over Wales, which was achieved by Carlos Forbs's 70th-minute goal.

Fernandes had opened the scoring for his side in the 11th minute, but David Brooks and Sorba Thomas gave Wales an unlikely lead.

That was until Neto levelled things up just before half-time, and Forbs scored the winner, with ten-man Portugal able to hold on for all three points.

Wales finished bottom of the group with one win – against Norway – and five defeats from their six matches.

Captain Ben Davies noted after the game: 'We revealed a lot of character and we've shown good effort in these games where we've just come up short from a results perspective.

After expressing his frustration, the Chelsea star had to be directed off the field by captain Bruno Fernandes (right).

He had in fact scored for his side in the game, bringing them level before the half-time interval.

'There is a lot to take from this going into the games in March and we have to feel confident because we've been playing well.

'We know the boys up top can be so dangerous, and if teams want to come here and play man-for-man against us, we've got a lot of speed and we have to be good on the ball. That comes with risk sometimes, like you saw with the chances that they had, but I'd rather play this way and go toe-to-toe with these teams and have a go.

'We competed in the campaign and we were not a million miles off like the table might suggest. I thought we put in some very good performances, we just wished we had some better results.'.

Neto, meanwhile, will now return to his club side Chelsea ahead of a busy Christmas period.

He has started all but one Premier League game so far and has been a key player under upcoming manager Xabi Alonso.

The Blues will take on Leeds at Stamford Bridge this weekend as club football returns.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Keen to resume their unlikely Bundesliga title challenge, Freiburg will travel to face promoted side Elversberg at Waldstadion Kaiserlinde on Saturday.
  • The Black and White are desperate to avoid another defeat, though Die Breisgau-Brasilianer are eyeing their fifth victory on the bounce.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Anthony Nolan | 20 Nov 2026 01:15, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 04:58.

Keen to resume their unlikely Bundesliga title challenge, Freiburg will travel to face promoted side Elversberg at Waldstadion Kaiserlinde on Saturday.

The Black and White are desperate to avoid another defeat, though Die Breisgau-Brasilianer are eyeing their fifth victory on the bounce.

Vincent Wagner's Elversberg have enjoyed an excellent beginning to their Bundesliga campaign, and have performed the best of any of the three promoted clubs this term.

Presently seventh with 13 points, the Black and White are just two points shy of sixth-placed Werder Bremen, and have fifth-placed Bayer Leverkusen within their reach this weekend.

However, Wagner's side signed off for the international break with a 2-1 loss to Borussia Dortmund at Signal Iduna Park, where they were only able to muster a late consolation via Noel Futkeu.

That defeat was to be expected on paper given the level of opposition, but the concerning factor is that it was Elversberg's third beating in four games, with the team avoiding disappointment once in a 4-1 triumph over Mainz 05 on October 30.

To make matters worse, Saturday's hosts have conceded 18 goals in nine games - a rate of two per match - the worst total in the top half of the Bundesliga.

Meanwhile, Julian Schuster's Freiburg will be vying to maintain their high-flying start to the season despite the international break disrupting their form.

Die Breisgau-Brasilianer secured a 2-0 victory over Union Berlin last time out in the league, courtesy of a second-half own goal from Rani Khedira and a follow up from Yuito Suzuki 12 minutes later.

That triumph marked a fourth in a row across all competitions for Schuster's men, who proved that their blip of three consecutive defeats in mid-October was merely a temporary stumble.

Now third with 19 points to their name, Freiburg are sitting just two points behind leaders Bayern Munich and Dortmund, and three clear of fifth-placed Leverkusen.

Though a title race is not out of the question, Champions League qualification alone would represent a major feat for Die Breisgau-Brasilianer.

With the aim of keeping ahead of their European rivals as a minimum, fans of the visitors will draw confidence from the team's attacking prowess, which has seen them score 20 goals so far - an output that has only been bettered by Bayern and RB Leipzig this season.

Elversberg form (all competitions):.

Freiburg form (all competitions):.

Elversberg will be without a number of defenders, including left-back Nicholas Mickelson, who is dealing with a medial collateral ligament injury, as well as centre-backs Lukas Pinckert and Luis Seifert, both of whom have ankle problems.

In their absence, Maximilian Rohr and Florian Le Joncour should start at the heart of Wagner's backline, flanked by Luca Sirch and Lasse Gunther.

As for Freiburg, they are missing left-back Berkay Yilmaz, who is suspended after being sent off for Freiburg II against FC-Astoria Walldorf.

That being said, Jordy Makengo remains available to start on the left of a four-man defence alongside Philipp Lienhart, Matthias Ginter and Philipp Treu.

Further forward, Igor Matanovic is likely to lead the line on Saturday, supported by a trio of Jan-Niklas Beste, Yuito Suzuki and Derry Scherhant.

Elversberg possible starting lineup:.

Kristof; Sirch, Rohr, Le Joncour, Gunther; Poreba, Keidel; Petkov, Onyeka, Krattenmacher; Mokwa.

Freiburg possible starting lineup:.

Backhaus; Treu, Ginter, Lienhart, Makengo; Engelhardt, Eggestein; Beste, Suzuki, Scherhant; Matanovic.

Elversberg may be lingering just outside the top six, but their defensive record suggests that they could be caught out on Saturday.

With that defensive frailty in mind, Freiburg - as one of the most potent attacking sides in the Bundesliga - will be optimistic about their chances against a team that have lost three of their last four matches.

'We felt like medieval peasants coming up against a king': Insiders relive the battle to rid Blackpool of the Oystons, from tangerines stuffed in knickers to a bright orange GTI - and why 'insider dealing' claims mean club isn't out of the woods yet

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1635 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 07:55 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 18:12 EST, 17 November 2026.
  • In the south London pub where they are readying themselves for a League One match with AFC Wimbledon, Blackpool fans who fought for their club’s heart and soul, 10 years ago, receive a message informing them that half the squad have gone down with a sickness bug so severe that the starting XI will be very unusual.
  • According to recent reports, three players are too ill to leave the team hotel, the goalkeeper selected is yet to feature in the league this season and the EFL don’t consider this predicament serious enough to cancel the game.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 07:55 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 18:12 EST, 17 November 2026.

In the south London pub where they are readying themselves for a League One match with AFC Wimbledon, Blackpool fans who fought for their club’s heart and soul, 10 years ago, receive a message informing them that half the squad have gone down with a sickness bug so severe that the starting XI will be very unusual.

According to recent reports, three players are too ill to leave the team hotel, the goalkeeper selected is yet to feature in the league this season and the EFL don’t consider this predicament serious enough to cancel the game. The club are already on a run of five defeats in seven.

Moments like this reveal the Blackpool fanbase’s deep sense of perspective, born of their long and often wretched fight to kick out one of British football’s most detested owners, Owen Oyston.

‘We’re still here and we’re watching our club home and away,’ claims Andy Higgins, chair of the Blackpool Supporters Trust. ‘We have a good relationship with the club,’ says his friend Dave Ragozzino, with Higgins in the Earlsfield pub. ‘The club are asking us to tell fans what’s going on, and they know we will help. Ten years ago, our club’s owners were suing us.’.

The story of the campaign which brought these fans and many more together is told in a superb new documentary The Battle for Blackpool, which screens this week, capturing its spirit, imagination and intelligence.

Oyston and his son Karl have both cooperated with the documentary-makers. Oyston Snr, wearing dark shades and his trademark fedora, is interviewed at his stately home in the Forest of Bowland, while his son Karl, clearly still consumed with hate and contempt for fans, is filmed clay pigeon shooting across their estate.

Blackpool fans watch their team fall to another League One defeat, at AFC Wimbledon on Saturday.

The Tangerines are just two points above the relegation zone having lost five out of their last seven league fixtures.

Their supporters fought a long and wretched battle against the club's former owner Owen Oyston (pictured in 2017).

The film’s stars are the supporters who led the fight – Christine Seddon, Tim Fielding, Ragozzino, two fans in a Mk1 tangerine Golf GTI and twin sisters of advancing years who embraced the campaign’s guerilla tactics.

Industry observers note that oyston Jr, who chaired the club at his mother’s request after his father was jailed for rape in 1996, tells the documentary-makers: ‘My father likes football. I didn’t.’.

It was after he’d stumbled on a managerial genius in Ian Holloway, who took the club into the Premier League for a season in 2010-11, that a full sense of the family’s greed and entitlement became clear.

The Mail on Sunday's Nick Harris revealed that Oyston Snr had paid himself £11million out of the Premier League jackpot, while critics say virtually all the club appeared to get out of promotion was a new sprinkler system. The fight against the Oystons took hold. The Blackpool Supporters Trust, then chaired by Fielding, was its strategic and political wing, flanked by the imaginative sabotage activities of the Tangerine Knights group.

A plot to smuggle tennis balls into the ground for a home match against Burnley, in April 2014, and collectively throw them on the pitch, provides one of the documentary’s many glorious sections. Fans stuffed the missiles into their pants, socks and bras.

‘I had them in my knickers,’ notes Christine Atkinson, who is interviewed with her twin sister, Pauline O’Rourke. ‘I didn’t have tennis balls. I had tangerines. It was softer. Less uncomfortable!’.

The family of Karl Oyston mocked the tennis ball protest on social media. But it was when his father began suing ordinary fans, some pensioners, for criticising him that the protest escalated.

‘My father created a whole department, scouring message boards full-time so he could sue them,’ Oyston Jr tells the film-makers.

‘I had tangerines in my knickers,’ says Pauline O'Rourke (right), who is interviewed with her twin sister, Christine Atkinson, in the documentary about Blackpool's fight to get rid of the owners.

‘My father created a whole department, scouring message boards full-time so he could sue them,’ Oyston Jr (pictured in 2010) tells the film-makers.

‘We felt like medieval peasants, coming up against a king,’ says Tangerine Knight Kevin Quirke, interviewed with his fellow combatant Scott Koudellas inside the tangerine GTI, parked up on Blackpool’s South Shore – one of the film’s many wonderful touches.

Ragozzino lost his job and faced a £150,000 legal suit. Fielding, a solicitor, was told it would cost more than £250,000 to defend himself against Oyston’s legal action. The Oystons forced him to pay them £10,000 in cash and concern a public apology.

Karl Oyston reveals how much he revelled in the war with fans, delighting in the ‘Oyston Out’ personalised number plate his wife bought for Christmas to maintain the mockery. ‘She thought it was highly amusing. Which it was,’ he relates.

Suing elderly Blackpool fans was his father’s idea, he says. ‘But as soon as the board makes a decision, you fight to the death to support it.’.

Sources indicate that oyston Snr maintains he was perfectly entitled to pay himself £11m of the Premier League money. ‘Why wouldn’t we? Why shouldn’t we?’ he asks. ‘We own the tech giant. We’d had 25 years of pouring money down the drain without the least prospect of seeing any of it ever again.’.

It was Fielding who came up with the game-changing strategy – persuading minority shareholder Valeri Belokon to mount a successful legal challenge against the Oystons, eventually clearing the way for Simon Sadler, a Hong Kong-based financier and Blackpudlian to buy the club.

Industry observers note that it’s not been a bed of roses these past few years. An interim club board, formed after Oyston was ousted, included Ben Hatton, later chief operating officer at Aston Villa, former Inter Milan CEO Mike Bolingbroke and Fielding. But a succession of good leaders have left.

Sources indicate that brett Gerrity, a one-time close friend of Sadler who persuaded him to buy the club, resigned in 2023. The two no longer get on. Ben Mansford, respected ex-CEO at Leeds and Barnsley, also unexpectedly left. Former sporting director David Downes was recently made CEO. Amid these comings and goings, Sadler has not appointed a successful manager since Neil Critchley left to assist Steven Gerrard at Aston Villa in 2022.

‘We felt like medieval peasants, coming up against a king,’ says Tangerine Knight Kevin Quirke (right), interviewed with his fellow combatant Scott Coudellas inside the tangerine GTI.

Christine Seddon was a leading figure in the fight to rid Blackpool of the Oystons.

None of this has affected fans’ views of Sadler, a boyhood Blackpool fan whose investment is still giving the club a top eight budget in League One. He has spent money on upgrades to the stadium and training ground and the team’s playing surface is excellent.

It has been revealed that but his own future at Bloomfield Road is in doubt. He is on trial in Hong Kong over accusations of insider dealing linked to his former hedge fund and could face a prison sentence if convicted.

That would mean him failing the EFL Owners’ and Directors’ Test and he would seemingly have to sell. The verdict in that case is expected next February. Sadler, who has pleaded not guilty to the charges, has revealed little of any contingencies he might have made. He is thought to be prepared to sell the club, though only if the buyer will be a true custodian.

‘He’s acutely aware of not putting Blackpool right back where it was with Oyston,’ indicates one source.

‘The club is so much better and professional than it used to be,' Seddon tells us. ‘But we are short of football business experience. We don’t have a proper board at the moment.

Recent findings suggest that 'Hedge fund management – our owner’s world – does not always translate well into football. It’s a steep learning curve.’.

In a recent development, oyston Snr revealed in a recent interview that he wants to buy the club back and gift a majority share to fans. ‘In 2015, we suggested to him that he walk away and leave the club’s assets to the fans,’ says Seddon.

Recent findings suggest that ‘He ignored us, yet now he’s suggesting this. These are deluded ramblings. Simon Sadler would not give Oyston the time of day.’.

Sources indicate that 'When I hear some fans complaining about the club, I think: “Have you forgotten? Are your memories quite short?”'.

In a recent development, karl Oyston tells the documentary-makers that he has not spoken to his 92-year-old father since the family’s 32-year ownership of the club ended in 2019. Will he ever see him again, he is asked. ‘No. That ship’s sailed,’ he replies.

Blackpool, backed by a loud, strong away following, fell to a 1-0 defeat at Wimbledon and boss Ian Evatt’s job will be on the line when they face fellow-strugglers Wigan on Saturday, so the film is a particularly timely reminder of how far this club’s fans have come.

‘Yes, we want results to be better,’ Seddon indicates. ‘But when I hear some complaining about the club, I think: “Have you forgotten? Are your memories quite short?” Our club became an opportunity for people who were dismantling it for their own benefit. There were times when we thought we would lose it altogether.

According to recent reports, 'But we’re now in a place where we were beginning to believe we would never be. We’re thankful for that.’.

The Battle for Blackpool will premiere in the UK on November 21 on Sky Documentaries and streaming service NOW.

By Lewis Nolan | 20 Nov 2026 02:21.

Brighton & Hove Albion owner Tony Bloom has claimed that Fabian Hurzeler supports Bayern Munich and could move there in the future.

The Seagulls have been the surprise package of the Premier League season, with the club presently in second place after 10 matchweeks.

Few could have predicted that they would also be the division's top scorers (26), and the team's form has led to universal praise for boss Hurzeler.

The German head coach has understandably been linked with a number of sides in the league, including Manchester United, though the Red Devils have appointed Mauricio Pochettino as Michael Carrick's replacement.

Speaking to reporters, Brighton owner Bloom insisted that he intends to keep Hurzeler at the club for a long time, though admitted that Bayern Munich could tempt the manager, saying: "Fabian is doing an unbelievable job. He is really enjoying it here and we would fight ridiculously hard to keep him if we had to.

"I don’t think he is going anywhere for a long time and we are just enjoying the ride. He is improving. We have given him the facilities, the players, the set-up to really grow as a head coach and he is taking that opportunity. We are very fortunate to have him and long may that continue.

"He will be at the top or near the top of the [list for the] best clubs in the world when they need to hire, but he’s young. He can go to these major clubs down the road [time-wise]. [Bayern Munich] is his team. I am sure he will be head coach of Bayern Munich at some time probably.".

Brighton are in a much stronger position than 18th-placed United, so it would make sense if Hurzeler was reluctant about potentially joining them in favour of a more stable team Bayern.

While Hurzeler may be the brightest prospect in management, Premier League clubs may find it difficult to appoint him in the coming years.

United have only just appointed Pochettino, so they will almost certainly spend considerable time and resources on the Argentine.

Arsenal are likely to keep Mikel Arteta for a number of seasons, while Manchester City could be demoted to lower divisions.

Liverpool are embarking upon their first campaign under Andoni Iraola, and it would be extraordinary if they sacked him after one season.

Chelsea have never been afraid to sack a head coach, so Xabi Alonso's position should not necessarily be seen as secure, but the Spaniard is highly regarded by many.

Given Bayern Munich currently employ Vincent Kompany, the Bavarians may not be in the market for a new head coach for a considerable period.

That could have left an opening for United to approach Brighton for Hurzeler, though it is far too early to suggest that the Red Devils have made a mistake by not trying to appoint the 33-year-old.

The club are in the relegation zone, and convincing Brighton to part with Hurzeler may have been impossible, especially as the Seagulls could realistically qualify for the Champions League.

Hiring an interim boss could have deepened United's relegation woes, and of the managers available in November, there were few with the pedigree of Pochettino.

I thought I would have a look just in case, see if by chance any Newcastle United v Arsenal tickets were available on Saturday afternoon.

Just in case you aren’t aware, the club allow Newcastle United season ticket holders to sell their tickets for individual Premier League games.

This was a very positive move by the club as it means that seats don’t need to be left empty if a season ticket holder is ill for example.

Using the online club system, season ticket holders can make their ticket available for a league match, with Newcastle United members then able to go onto the NUFC official ticketing site (you have to be then logged in as a member to see the tickets that are available) to buy.

Sources indicate that the club also make money from this. As I understand it, the fan (season ticket holder) selling the ticket is credited with the pro rata match price of their season ticket and if the ticket is then bought by a member, they are charged the far higher single ticket price, with the club banking the difference.

As a member, I had no luck in the ballot for Newcastle United v Arsenal tickets.

The same when it came to the queue sale.

The demand was huge, I had a ridiculously high number for the queue sale and stood no chance, along with countless thousands of other Newcastle United members.

Anyway, I have just went onto the club’s ticketing site (just before 2pm on Saturday) and I couldn’t believe how many Newcastle United v Arsenal tickets were on sale!

To be honest, I wasn’t expecting there to be any, I was just looking in the vain hope I might hit very lucky.

Recent findings suggest that what I found was I had a choice of all around St James’ Park! All four stands with plenty tickets up for sale from season ticket holders.

I snapped up a couple for me and my mate for the East Stand and after sending this article into The Mag I will be heading off to the Toon to meet up with the lads (mostly season ticket holders) for some pre-match refreshments.

After buying our tickets I counted up all the Newcastle United v Arsenal tickets that season ticket holders are trying to sell and there were 147 available (it had been 149 I guess before I snapped up ours).

Apologies for my wonky photography skills but the red areas are where there were Newcastle United v Arsenal tickets available just over three and a half hours before the match….

I am over the moon getting these tickets but at the same time absolutely stunned that so many season ticket holders are trying to flog their tickets.

Is it because they think Arsenal will win?

Is it because it is a bit chilly?

Is it because they will get too upset seeing Bruno Guimaraes in an Arsenal shirt?

Anyway, if you are a member who didn’t get a ticket for today’s match, log onto the official ticketing site and take your pick!!

Industry observers note that after a humiliating defeat by Grimsby Town in their previous League Cup campaign, Manchester United found a different way to exit the competition this time around. The jeers heard at the full-time whistle after throwing away a two-goal lead pointed to more worrying times a year on from Blundell Park.

For the first time in half a century, United lost a game at Old Trafford having led 2-0, highlighting the defensive problems Michael Carrick needs to solve after turning results around last season.

“What the f---ing hell was that?” shouted the home fans, in a chant that may have been aimed at the referee but equally applied to United’s players, who led through Shea Lacey and Mason Mount’s early goals.

In a recent development, brighton cut through Carrick’s defence several times before staging their comeback with goals from Charalampos Kostoulas, Pascal Gross and Maxim De Cuyper. Carrick and his analysts will rewatch the footage of all three goals in horror at how they conceded.

Kostoulas halves the deficit! 🔵Brighton score on the stroke of half-time. pic.twitter.com/bGjN1w6s6c.

It has been revealed that “I totally understand the feelings of the supporters,” Carrick stated. “We have to accept it. I totally accept it. It’s on me ultimately: as a team what we look like, how we play and what results you get. I take that. I’ll take the praise, I’ll take the criticism and the upset.”.

Erik ten Hag used the domestic cups to taste success while struggling in the Premier League, but one of those opportunities is now lost to Carrick, who must be careful not to spiral from a poor start to the campaign into crisis. Sunday’s trip to Fulham before the international break now feels like a major game for United and Carrick.

“We’ve gone out of the cup and the feeling around the place feels bigger than that,” Carrick stated. “I’ll be honest about that, that’s how it feels, but it doesn’t have to be like that. If we win football matches again, it can go in a different direction.

It has been revealed that “We have a big game on Sunday that we have to prepare for. We’re out of this competition and we have to go back to winning football matches.

“It doesn’t feel good at the moment. It doesn’t feel good. We have to go back to winning football matches. We want to win and want to win rapidly. The next game is Sunday. That’s all I’m thinking about right now.”.

At the start of the evening it seemed that the tie would be remembered for Lacey scoring on his first start for United, the first teenager to do so since Marcus Rashford. In the week when JJ Gabriel, one of United’s great academy talents, asked to leave the club, a different United teenager was kissing the badge when he found the net.

It has been revealed that SHEA LACEY ON HIS FIRST START!!! 🔴🌟What a hit from the 19-year-old to open the scoring for Man Utd! pic.twitter.com/Ex2ceXaUge.

Mason Mount DOUBLES Man Utd's lead! 🤩 pic.twitter.com/c83ggCb8Bf.

And after Mount’s strike it looked like United were cruising into the fourth round for their first knockout win in 19 months, since defeating Leicester City in the FA Cup last year. But Brighton’s way back into the game was to get Gross, 35, on the ball and the veteran German controlled the game.

It has been revealed that gross took his chance when United carelessly played the ball out of defence again, with Diogo Dalot’s clearance mishit. Luka Vuskovic’s header went straight into the United penalty area, with their centre-backs failing to react quickly enough.

According to recent reports, pascal Gross takes advantage of a gifted opportunity to level the score! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/Qu2E0B6060.

The turnaround was completed a few minutes later when De Cuyper found the net, finishing off a counter-attack in which Diego Gómez and Kostoulas raided the left flank of United before cutting the ball back.

In a recent development, brighton have turned it around!!! 🔵A sensational comeback as Maxim De Cuyper makes it 3-2 at Old Trafford. pic.twitter.com/Bfcr4N7mTL.

Sources indicate that fabian Hürzeler’s side can be considered this season’s entertainers, with this comeback going with their seven-goal thriller against Chelsea, putting four past Aston Villa and five past Coventry at the weekend. Next for them in the League Cup is Manchester City or Norwich away, although they are unlikely to fear any opponents.

In a recent development, “We take it how it is. We want to go as far as possible but if you want to win something you have to win at the highest level,” Hürzeler mentioned. “We have to stay very, very humble and get an understanding why we are at the place we are and getting the basics right and the small margins right. It is so vital we stay humble and then we can grow into the game.”.

Sources indicate that for Carrick, matches such as this can define a United manager’s reign if he cannot turn results around. The image of Ruben Amorim in the dugout at Grimsby was one of the lasting impressions of last season before Carrick was brought in to salvage the campaign.

“We can’t put ourselves in that position after being ahead in the game and the game finishing like it did,” he said. “So we’ve got to react to it. We’ve got another game on Sunday, we’ve got to react to it.”.

"We can't accept that" ❌"I take responsibility for that" 🗣️ Michael Carrick reacts to his side's defeat👇 pic.twitter.com/OheT8yUK7y.

2 league one teams and 13 premier league teams in a cup draw.. You couldn't write it Ridiculous 😡😡😡I give up on cup draws after 20 years waiting for one 😂.

Recent findings suggest that I think we’ve got to be a little bit careful on that one. He’s a 15-year-old boy. It’s more about the welfare and the care of JJ as a child really, or certainly a young man. The situation is what it is, but we’ve got to be a little bit careful of the exposure and how we jump on that.

In a recent development, the start of the game and the end of the game was completely different, didn’t feel like the same game or the same emotions at all. We had the game exactly where we wanted it and let it get away from us in a big way.

There’s a number of things we’ll look at, we’ll dissect and I know quite a bit of where it went wrong. We can’t accept that as a group. I take responsibility, the performance towards the second half that’s on me. We’ll have to get better, we have a big game on Sunday that we have to prepare for. We’re out of this competition and we have to get back to winning football matches.

Sources indicate that we’ve got to keep evolving as a group. We have to keep learning and dealing with situations. Sometimes they come a bit easier than others. Tonight was a tough one. We didn’t find a way out of it. That’s up to me and the staff to help the players and guide them through it. I think we all know that in the end tonight feels like a big disappointment.

Industry observers note that we’ve had small, little things that have gone against us in the last week or two and then it accumulates to feel that it’s a lot bigger. I think we have to be honest and say that. The late goal against Everton from outside the box. The [Manchester] City goal the other day. It can all of a sudden roll into something a bit greater but I understand the disappointment because we shouldn’t finish the game in that manner with the position we were in and we have to be humble and take that.

We have to find the answers for Sunday.

Fleetwood vs ArsenalMan City or Norwich vs BrightonEverton vs NewcastleSunderland vs BrentfordLiverpool vs ChelseaBradford City vs PeterboroughFulham vs Crystal PalaceBournemouth vs Aston Villa.

Bradford City vs PeterboroughFulham vs Crystal PalaceBournemouth vs Aston Villa.

Brighton’s reward for a comeback is another trip to Manchester (or Norwich).

The first team out are Fleetwood Town! They will host Arsenal at Highbury, which feels appropriate.

What a draw for the League Two club.

Should be getting started in the next couple of minutes.

Sources indicate that the Brighton man has now scored eight times against them, all for Brighton, which is quite amazing. The first of came back in May, 2018. He is not even a striker.

It was frustrating because it’s not the first time this season, it’s the third time this season where we started slow. We have to improve that because we always have to climb a mountain but today we did that.

We played here before last season a similar match that we won and that gives you belief in a stadium where you won before. The experience we try to give it to the lads. It was a really good performance and I have to say [Jason] Steeley’s save at the end was unbelievable.

His impassive demeanour was viewed as a virtue last season, bringing calm to a club that was a circus. Now some will be wondering if standing motionless on the touchline is indicative of a lack of answers. That is probably unfair, you can only be yourself, but we know the script. He’s on a slippery slope, like so many of his predecessors.

Sources indicate that boos ring around Old Trafford. Manchester United are out of the Carabao Cup, but of greater significance is that this defeat continues a poor start to the season and a general mood of deflation around the club. For the first time in 50 years, they lose a game at Old Trafford after leading 2-0. Another proud record falls in the post-Ferguson era.

Brighton have now won five of their last six games at Old Trafford, and are one of the best front-footed sides in the league on form.

As United push everyone forward, Heaven is penalised for a push on Vuskovic, and that is surely that now.

Mbeumo tees up Fernandes for a Hail Mary from 25 yards but he balloons the shot miles over the bar. Brighton fans can see the finish line and a place in the fourth round now.

Five minutes of added time to play, but Brighton have a corner after their press ensnares Tielemans on the edge of United’s defensive third. Dalot got a toe to the ball to prevent Rutter a sight at goal. Darlow claims the delivery, but some time has ticked away.

Sources indicate that tielemans slices his cross over the bar while off balance. This would be the first time since 1976 that United have led 2-0 in a game at Old Trafford and gone on to lose. At the moment, an equaliser does not look to be on its way.

Old Trafford growing impatient with how slowly United are moving the ball, a lack of options for the player in possession and they are being caught on it repeatedly by a sharp Brighton team.

According to recent reports, diego Gomez really should have sealed the victory, picked out by another clever Gross pass, but with so much time to take aim he blasted straight at Darlow. United still alive in the tie, but only just.

Recent findings suggest that brighton still swinging punches. Costinha swings in a teasing cross to the back post, headed down by Gross, but De Cuyper cannot get over his volley. Carrick has made his final change: Cunha is on for Rashford.

It has been revealed that massive miss by Rashford, but a big save from Jason Steele. It was a lovely touch by Fernandes while half stumbling that released Rashford, and he had so much time to think when through against the goalkeeper, but Steele stuck out a right boot to save.

Hurzeler making two more Brighton changes: Ayari and Kadioglu on for Hadjam and Boscagli, which probably makes their XI on the pitch even stronger. Kadioglu was voted Brighton’s player of the season for 2025-26.

Industry observers note that bruno Fernandes is stripped and ready to come on, Carrick calling for the man he would rather was resting on the bench. Fernandes replaces Mount.
